  • Perfect Balance (20 points): When using the weapon in dual wielding, you can perform a dual wield attack with your other weapon, even when making a heavy or precise attack with this weapon.
  • Surprise Weapon (35 points): The weapon is designed to look like a mundane object.  Each Combat, after you draw the weapon, if the next attack you make that round is using this weapon and is a basic light or heavy attack it gains the Trick Attack keyword.  After benefitting from this bonus, you cannot do so again the same combat even if drawing a different weapon with with Surprise Weapon or Hidden Weapon.
  • Versatile (10 points): Can be added to a 1h weapon from a group that also has an option to be a 2h weapon (ie Axe, but not small weapons). Increases the burden of the weapon by 1, but the weapon can be used as either a one-handed or two-handed weapon. Must declare which version you are using at the start of your turn, before you making any attacks with this weapon.

B mods:

  • Perfect Edge (25 points): An accuracy roll of 20 gains Sure Hit. If you roll a 20 and choose to have this apply, any Full Pierce is removed from the attack.
  • Momentum (25 points): After downing or killing an enemy, you may Sidestep up to your speed towards another enemy as part of that action.
  • Gathering II (80 points): This weapon gives a +1 bonus to gathering rolls its used in. Stacks with Gathering mod.

Alloy Mods:

Alloy mods can also be put on any weapon, but require the weapon to include a specific type of alloy. If the weapon does not include this alloy, the mod cannot be used.

  • Arcanium
    • Barrier Weaving (A mod, 20 points): When you apply a Shield to an ally or yourself, your shield is treated as if the stat it scales off is 1 higher. (If it doesn’t scale off a stat, there is no effect)
  • Salachar
    • Burning Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round inflicts Burning 18 to the target on damage until the start of your next turn.
  • Ghimslag:
    • Slowing Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round slows the target on damage until the start of your next turn.
  • Fulgorite:
    • Thundering Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round inflicts Static 18 to the target on damage.
    • Conductor (B mod, 50 points):  When this weapon deals Lightning damage against a soaked target, it gains Half Pierce.
  • Luxaeterna:
    • Shining Weapon (A mod, 10 points): Your weapon emits a bright light in a 60ft radius. Can be enabled or disabled for 1 AP.
    • Healer Weapon (A mod, 20 points): When you heal an ally or yourself, you heal as if your power (or focus, agility or toughness if the heal scales off those) was 1 higher.
    • Undead Slayer (B mod, 50 points): When this weapon deals holy damage, it always deals Full Pierce damage against undead unless the undead resists Holy damage.
    • Shielding Healer (B mod, 50 points): When you cast a healing spell that costs mana, the target(s) of your spell gain Temporary HP equal to your Toughness until the start of your next turn.
  • Sylphsteel:
    • Pushing Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round pushes the target back 10ft on damage.
  • Corvuskite:
    • Stealth Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first attack of an encounter does not break stealth if made with this weapon.
    • Darkness Weapon (B mod, 80 points): If the first basic attack on your turn made with this weapon deals damage, you may immediately hide from the target (but not other enemies) even if you’re not in cover.
  • Glacite
    • Slowing Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round slows the target on damage until the start of your next turn.

Flamellon Mods:

Flamellon mods are special mods that can be put on weapons. To put one of these mods on an item you must have sufficient items with the matching Flamelic Polarity.

  • Aetherplumes (feathers/wings with high magic concentration. Tengu/Harpy/Fae etc):
    • Aerial Supremacy (A mod, 30 points, 1500 Aetherplume polarity): You gain +1 accuracy against flying creatures.
    • Aerial Takedown (B mod, 50 points, 2500 Aetherplume polarity): If you damage a flying creature and it would lose altitude from taking damage, the altitude they lose is doubled.
  • Insectoid (Fae Cicada Shell):
    • Dazing Strike (B mod, 80 points, 6000 Insect Polarity): If your first basic attack of a round deals damage, the target becomes Dazed.
    • Distracting Strike (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Insect Polarity): If your first basic attack of a round deals damage, the target loses any concentration effect they have.
  • Plant Materials (Yggdrassil Seed):
    • Vine Grab (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Plant Polarity): If your first basic attack of a round deals damage to an enemy that's slowed, that target becomes rooted until the start of your next turn.
  • Poison Materials (Toxic Core):
    • Poison Weapon (A mod, 10 points, 2000 Poison Polarity): You deal Poison damage with this weapon.
    • Venom Drip (A mod, 30 points, 1500 Poison Polarity): You deal 1 Full Pierce Earth(Poison) damage on hit. (This extra damage does not trigger effects that normally trigger on damage).
    • Poisoned Sheath (B mod, 25 points, 1250 Poison Polarity): You may apply a poison to your sheath. When you draw the weapon, the poison is automatically applied to the weapon.
  • Gravity Materials (Gravity Orb): 
    • Gravity Disruption (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Gravity Polarity): When you deal damage to a target with this weapon, the target suffers a -4 penalty to all ranged attacks until the start of your next turn. Can only be added to a melee weapon and does not apply when the target you were attacking with the weapon was more than 10ft away from you.
  • Spidersilk:
    • Sticky Weapon (B mod, 50 points, 2000 Spidersilk Polarity): Once per turn when you make a basic attack against an enemy you may choose to have your weapon stick to them on hit. While you are stuck to them, you move along with them if the target chooses to move unless they spend 2 AP to remove the weapon from you. While stuck to the target, the weapon cannot be used to make attacks. Can only be added to a melee weapon.

items.name: Wand (One-Handed)
items.description:
Magic Blast: You may alter the damage type fired by an attack made with this weapon for 0 AP. The damage type must be an element type you have mastered (usually unlocked through classes) or one that’s built into the weapon. Each weapon has at least one element built in.

Range: 60ft

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Ornamental (10 points): You may use this weapon as one minor item such as an instrument or parasol.
    • Echo Blast (20 points): When you make a basic Heavy attack, you may split the damage against two different targets in range. Make only 1 accuracy check against both.
    • Warding Wand (35 points): You may spend 1 AP to gain 5 temporary HP until the start of your next turn.
  • B mods:
    • Dedicated Focus (50 points): Gain +1 bonus to accuracy rolls, but can only fire elemental attacks of 1 element. Spells cast through this wand only gain that bonus if they deal that element of damage.
    • Mana Core (80 points): When you deal max damage with an attack made with this weapon or with a spell cast through this weapon against an enemy in an encounter, your next spell this turn costs 1 less mana (min 0)

items.name: Wand (Two-Handed)
items.description:
Magic Blast: You may alter the damage type fired by an attack made with this weapon for 0 AP. The damage type must be an element type you have mastered (usually unlocked through classes) or one that’s built into the weapon. Each weapon has at least one element built in.

Range: 120ft

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Ornamental (10 points): You may use this weapon as one minor item such as an instrument or parasol.
    • Echo Blast (20 points): When you make a basic Heavy attack, you may split the damage against two different targets in range. Make only 1 accuracy check against both.
    • Warding Wand (35 points): You may spend 1 AP to gain 5 temporary HP until the start of your next turn.
  • B mods:
    • Mana Surge (25 points): Once per round after you cast a spell, you may make a Light attack for 0 AP. Two-Handed wand only. This counts as your dual wield attack.
    • Dedicated Focus (50 points): Gain +1 bonus to accuracy rolls, but can only fire elemental attacks of 1 element. Spells cast through this wand only gain that bonus if they deal that element of damage.
    • Mana Core (80 points): When you deal max damage with an attack made with this weapon or with a spell cast through this weapon against an enemy in an encounter, your next spell this turn costs 1 less mana (min 0)

items.name: Water Balloon
items.description:
A flask that when thrown explodes in a 5ft radius around the target and applies Soaked 5 to all targets in the area. May be thrown up to 40ft away.

Crafting:
Materials: 200 Alchemy Materials
Herbs:

  • 1x Common Water

items.name: Weak Spider Poison
items.description:
Contact Poison. Can be applied to a weapon. Lasts for 2 hits or 1 minute (6 rounds).

When an attack with this poison damages an enemy, they become Dazed. If an enemy is already dazed, they instead take 8 full pierce Poison damage. An enemy can only be affected by this poison (daze and damage effect both apply) twice per round.

Crafting:
Materials: 300 Alchemy Materials
Special Materials:

  • 150 units of Spidersilk

items.name: Weak Wyvern Poison
items.description:
Contact Poison. Can be applied to a weapon. Lasts for 1 hits or 1 minute (6 rounds).

When an attack with this poison damages an enemy, they become poisoned. The next time they move the full distance they can in an action they take, they take 3d6 full pierce Poison damage.

Crafting:
Materials: 230 Alchemy Materials
Special Materials:

  • 2 Common Earth Herbs

items.name: Web Flask
items.description:
A flask that when thrown coats a 20x20 feet area in sticky webs until the start of your next turn. Anyone walking through it becomes Slowed and any creature ending its turn inside of it becomes Rooted until the start of their next turn. May be thrown up to 40ft away.

Crafting:
Materials: 400 Alchemy Materials
Herbs:

  • 1x Rare Wind
  • 1x Rare Earth

items.name: Whip (One-Handed)
items.description:
Whip Crack: You gain +5ft range on your weapon attacks. Weapon attacks made at max range (default of 10) gain +1 damage. Your threatened range is still 5ft.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Barbed Wire (10 points): Upon landing a critical hit with this weapon, apply Bleeding to the target.
    • Fluttering Ribbon (35 points): At the start of your turn, you may change your threatened range to 5-10ft until the start of your next turn.
  • B mods:
    • Binding Flow (50 points): When dealing damage with a Heavy attack, you may choose to not do damage to instead reduce a creature’s movement speed to 0 until the start of your next turn or until you move. Does not work against bosses or creatures bigger than you.
    • Hooked Coil (80 points): When dealing damage with an attack of opportunity against an enemy leaving your range, you may pull them back 5ft. Only triggers once per turn.

items.name: Wind Bubble
items.description:
A simple device that can be attached to the body or held in the hand. When activated, it creates a bubble of wind around the wielder that slows down falling speed to 40ft per round. If the wearer reaches the ground while in this bubble, they take no fall damage.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Quick Activation (20 points): The activation cost is reduced by 1 AP or 1 RP, to a minimum of 0.
  • B mods:
    • Slow Fall (25 points): Reduces the falling speed down to 20ft per round.
    • Underwater Mode (50 points): If used underwater, the bubble provided you air as you slowly float upwards.

items.name: Winged Backpack
items.description:
A backpack that looks ordinary at a first glance. It can store the same amount of items as a normal backpack. When activated, a pair of mechanical wings fold out. While the wings are out, you slow down your falling speed to 15ft per round and you are able to move horizontally as if normally moving. If you hit the ground while they are active, you do not take any falling damage. Lasts for 5 minues or until you hit the ground.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Quick Activation (20 points): The activation cost is reduced by 1 AP, to a minimum of 0.
  • B mods:
    • Hover Mode (80 points): When activated, the wearer can fly at half speed up to a maximum of 40ft high. If activated when higher than 40ft high, you glide down until you reach the 40ft height limit. Functions similarly to the Flight ability in regards to taking damage while flying.

items.name: Wolf
items.description:
A wolf trained to be used in combat.

 

Stats:

HP: 20

Focus: 4

Power: 4

Agility: 3

Toughness: 3

Speed: 25ft

Size: Large

 

Special qualities:

Topple Prey: You may spend 2 AP to command your mount to make a Light attack against the target. On damage, the target is knocked prone. This attack uses your mount’s stats instead of your own and it gains a +2 to hit for every ally (apart from you) within 5ft of the target.

items.name: Wolverine Elixir
items.description:
An elixir that prevents non-lethal injuries.  When drunk, you take 11 true damage. Until the end of the encounter, you do not suffer any injuries, except for a Mortal Wound (you can still lose HP and still become downed when reaching 0 HP). 

Crafting:
Materials: 2050 Alchemy Materials
Herbs:

  • 1x Mystic Earth
  • 1x Rare Fire

items.name: Wyvern
items.description:
A wyvern trained to be ridden by people.

 

Stats:

HP: 75

Focus: 4

Power: 6

Agility: 3

Toughness: 6

Speed: 40ft

Size: Large

 

Special qualities:

Flying Mount: Your mount can fly. While flying you may only move in a straight line when making a movement action. While moving only on the ground, your speed is reduced to 20ft but this restriction does not apply.

In flight vulnerability: When your mount takes damage while flying, its height is lowered by 20ft. If this would reduce its height to the ground level, it becomes rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn.

Breath Weapon: You may spend 1 AP to make your mount use a breath weapon (damage type dependent on the wyrm type), making a Light attack against all enemies in a 30ft cone. This attack uses your mount’s stats instead of your own

items.name: XL Healing Potion
items.description:
Healing liquid in a vial made from various herbs and reagents. Spurs the body’s natural healing by converting mana into regeneration.  Much purer and more difficult to create, uses special materials. When drank, you heal for 45 HP.

Crafting:
Materials: 1800 Alchemy Materials
Herbs:

  • 1x Mystic Fire

keywords.name: Active
keywords.description: You cannot use the Prepare action on this ability.

keywords.name: Aid
keywords.description: Abilities with the Aid keyword can only be used on allies, unless the ability specifically states you can use it on yourself.

keywords.name: Artillery
keywords.description: The attack can target non-hidden units behind cover (even full cover) and any cover is calculated from above the target rather than from your position to the target.

keywords.name: Augment
keywords.description: An attack that has been modified by an Augment effect cannot be modified again and given another Augment effect.

keywords.name: Blanketing
keywords.description: When you make an attack against multiple targets with this ability, roll one accuracy and damage check that applies against all targets.

keywords.name: Bleeding
keywords.description: You take 1d6 true damage at the start of your turn.

keywords.name: Blinded
keywords.description: Blinded characters suffer a -X penalty to their accuracy rolls where X is the blinded value. If they are Blinded for 3 or higher, they cannot make any ranged attacks without first locating a target through another means than sight. If they are blinded for 5 or higher, they also cannot gain Sure Hit on their attacks.

keywords.name: Block Crush
keywords.description: Block Crush attacks ignore any additional Guard gained from the Block action.

keywords.name: Broken
keywords.description: Only applies to equipment. Armor and shields that are broken provide no benefit or negatives. Weapons that are broken can only be used as an improvised weapon.

keywords.name: Burning
keywords.description: A Burning character takes X damage at the end of their turn. They may spend 1 AP to remove this effect.

keywords.name: Challenge
keywords.description:
If a challenged character does not include the challenger as a target when making an attack, they provoke a melee attack of opportunity from the challenger.

This does not trigger if the challenged target makes an attack of opportunity or if the challenger is not a target due effects such as charm.

keywords.name: Charm
keywords.description: You may not willingly target the charmer with attacks unless you have no other valid targets (excluding allies) for the attack. Your AoE abilities that target allies also include the charmer, and your AoE attacks or abilities that exclude allies also exclude the charmer.

keywords.name: Circuit
keywords.description: The first time each combat you use an ability with this keyword, the mana cost is reduced by 1. Afterwards, this mana cost reduction is removed from all abilities with this keyword.

keywords.name: Combo
keywords.description: Combo abilities gain a bonus when used directly after another ability. Combo abilities remain valid until you spend AP on a different ability or action.

keywords.name: Concentration
keywords.description: A character can only have 1 Concentration effect active at the same time. They may drop a Concentration effect during their turn for 0 AP. When a character gets Downed, they lose Concentration.

keywords.name: Crushing
keywords.description: On an unblocked hit, this attack deals a minimum damage equal to your Power.

keywords.name: Daze
keywords.description: You immediately lose 1 AP. If you do not have any AP, you instead regen 1 less AP at the start of your next turn. A dazed target becomes immune to Daze until the end of their next turn.

keywords.name: Disarm
keywords.description: When disarmed, you cannot make weapon attacks with the weapon you were wielding when you got disarmed. You must draw the weapon again to use it when the Disarm ends. Unarmed attacks are unaffected by Disarm.

keywords.name: Divine
keywords.description: If you took the Divine's Chosen breakthrough, this ability's damage type becomes your chosen divine's damage type instead of Holy.

keywords.name: Domain
keywords.description: A domain area spell. Only one domain area may be active at a location at a time.

keywords.name: Enchantment
keywords.description: An enchantment is placed on a weapon. A weapon can only have 1 enchantment at the same time. If an enchantment is placed on a channeling weapon, it transfer the enchantment properties to any spells cast while holding it.

keywords.name: Esoteric Art
keywords.description: You can only use 1 ability with this keyword or with the Secret Art keyword per encounter.

keywords.name: Expose
keywords.description:
The target's crit threshold is reduced by the expose value (base 1, reducing normal crit threshold from 20→19). Stacks with katana's reduced crit threshold and other abilities which lower the crit threshold of the user.

Expose is removed once the target is critically hit (regardless of if they defend or not)

keywords.name: Fire
keywords.description: Spells and attacks that deal Fire damage may ignite flammable, unattended objects.

keywords.name: Flashback
keywords.description: Flashbacks are abilities that refer to an earlier time in the campaign. They reflect prior planning that the character has made to affect the current situation.

keywords.name: Full Pierce
keywords.description: Full pierce attacks cannot be reduced by guard.

keywords.name: Half Pierce
keywords.description: Half Pierce attacks ignore Guard, unless the target takes the Block action or Dodge action.

keywords.name: Half Rapid
keywords.description: This ability may be used once on each creature every round.

keywords.name: Hellfire
keywords.description:
Hellfire functions like Burning (You take X damage at the end of your turn), but it can no longer be removed the normal way if not removed before the end of the target’s next turn. It can still be dispelled through the use of abilities.

Hellfire can be applied to enemies immune to Burning, but it can still be removed like normal even after a turn has passed. Hellfire is automatically removed at the end of the encounter.

keywords.name: Hiding
keywords.description: While in Hiding, enemies cannot see or target you and even if they are aware of your presence, they cannot pinpoint your exact location. You lose Hiding if you move, attack or use any other ability that does not have the Stealth keyword unless that movement or attack says otherwise.

keywords.name: Illumination
keywords.description: The next attack against you gets an X bonus to the accuracy roll (Consumed even on a miss).

keywords.name: Immovable
keywords.description: While not flying, effects from other creatures that knock you prone or force you to move such as knockbacks are ineffective.

keywords.name: Instant
keywords.description: Can be used while another action is resolving to temporarily interrupt it. The Instant ability resolves immediately and before any interrupted ability can resolve. The current action is cancelled and refunded if the target becomes invalid.

keywords.name: Isolated
keywords.description: If you have no allies within 10ft of you and at least 2 enemies within 10ft of you, you are considered Isolated.

keywords.name: Killing Blow
keywords.description:
Killing Blow effects trigger when reducing the HP of enemy to 0 or lower.

You cannot benefit from the same Killing Blow effect against the same target more than once.

keywords.name: Lock On
keywords.description: Lock On attacks ignore the bonus from dodge.

keywords.name: Lockstep
keywords.description: This attack always matches the target's base evasion (including bonuses etc, but they may still dodge it like normal).

keywords.name: Miracle
keywords.description: A character may only cast 1 Miracle per encounter.

keywords.name: Mystic Eye
keywords.description: This ability is made with a Mystic Eye.

keywords.name: Ninjutsu
keywords.description: This ability requires two free hands. You may wield Small weapon, Saboteur threaded dagger, One-handed thrown and Sets of Missiles weapons and still count as having your hand free.

keywords.name: Offstep
keywords.description: Attacks against you always meet your base evasion (Including bonuses etc, but you may still dodge them like normal).

keywords.name: Opener
keywords.description: This ability can only be used as the first action in a turn. (Paying upkeep does not count as an action)

keywords.name: Opportunistic
keywords.description: You may use this ability instead of making a regular of attack of opportunity. This ability is counted as making an attack of opportunity and you don't get your regular one if you use it.

keywords.name: Overcharge
keywords.description: You may spend additional AP and/or Mana to increase the power of the ability.

keywords.name: Pass
keywords.description: You can move through enemy units for this movement.

keywords.name: Persist
keywords.description:
This effect costs +X mana to dispel. If the creature dispelling it does not use mana, it takes +X AP (or +X RP) instead.

Does not apply when they use the natural way of removing it, if possible (For example by spending 1 AP to remove a Burn).

keywords.name: Pinpoint
keywords.description: You ignore points of the target's guard equal to your Focus. Cannot reduce guard below 0.

keywords.name: Presence Concealment
keywords.description: You hide your mana output and aura, making it harder to detect you by magical means—Causing your spirit core to be considered 0 for the purposes of detection and aura abilities.  In addition you gain a +5 bonus to stealth.

keywords.name: Prone
keywords.description: An ability with this keyword can be used while Prone with no penalty. All attacks without the Prone keyword cost +1 AP and RP while prone.

keywords.name: Quick
keywords.description: The first time after using an ability with Quick, other abilities with Quick used in same turn cost +1 AP.

keywords.name: Rage
keywords.description: This ability can be used while in Rage Stance.

keywords.name: Rapid
keywords.description: This ability can be used more than once per turn.

keywords.name: Regrowth
keywords.description: You heal for 3+Focus (of the one who applied it) at the start of your turn.

keywords.name: Root
keywords.description: You cannot move and your evasion when taking the Dodge reaction is changed to 13 + Agility (rounded down)

keywords.name: Safe
keywords.description: This spell and/or attack does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

keywords.name: Sanctify
keywords.description:
Attacks against you that hit heal an enemy attacker by 3+the applier's focus. After this triggers, the stacks of this debuff are reduced by 1.

An attacker at full HP may choose not to trigger the effect.

keywords.name: Scatter
keywords.description: When you make an attack against multiple targets with this ability, roll a separate accuracy and damage check against each target.

keywords.name: Secret Art
keywords.description: You can only use 1 ability with this keyword or with the Esoteric Art keyword per encounter.

keywords.name: Setup
keywords.description: Setup attacks can be completed by spending AP in the following turn. While charging the attack, no other AP actions can be taken and attacks against you gain the Trick Attack keyword. You may cancel a setup attack instead of finishing it and don't need to spend the remaining AP. Setup attacks cannot activate before the start of your next turn and you cannot use the Prepare action on Setup abilities. You may cancel a setup attack at any time by spending 0 RP. You must spend at least 1 AP to begin charging a setup attack.

keywords.name: Shaken
keywords.description: The target's maximum AP is reduced by 1.

keywords.name: Shieldbreaker
keywords.description: This attack deals double damage to the HP of Shields and Temporary HP. Any carryover damage is not doubled.

keywords.name: Sickened
keywords.description: When making a roll that uses Focus, Power, Agility or Toughness, they are treated as 1 lower.

keywords.name: Sidestep
keywords.description: Your movement does not provoke attacks of opportunities.

keywords.name: Slow
keywords.description: Your movement speed is halved.

keywords.name: Soaked
keywords.description: A soaked target takes X additional damage when taking Lighting damage.

keywords.name: Song
keywords.description: A character can only have 1 Song active at the same time.

keywords.name: Sound
keywords.description: This ability's effect is based around sound. Those who can't hear it are unaffected.

keywords.name: Spell
keywords.description: This ability is considered a spell. Unless stated otherwise, it will provoke attacks of opportunity.

keywords.name: Stacking
keywords.description: Abilities with this keyword give stacks of something. You can only gain stacks of 1 thing with this keyword a the same time. Upon gaining a stack of a different kind, your original stacks are lost.

keywords.name: Stagger
keywords.description: A character inflicted with Stagger has their evasion reduced by X, where X is the Stagger value.

keywords.name: Stance
keywords.description: Only 1 Stance ability can be active at the same time.

keywords.name: Static
keywords.description: At the end of your next turn, you deal X lightning damage to all allies within 5ft of you.

keywords.name: Stealth
keywords.description: This ability does not pull you out of Hiding. You must still be in low cover after using this ability to remain in Hiding.

keywords.name: Strafe
keywords.description: You must have moved at least the Strafe distance towards the target before making an attack with this keyword.

keywords.name: Stun
keywords.description: Your AP, AP recovery and RP is set to 0 when afflicted by this. When it ends, you regain any unused RP lost from this effect.

keywords.name: Summon
keywords.description:
This ability counts towards your maximum summon limit. You can only have 2 summons active at the same time.

A summon does not count as a valid target for abilities that require a ‘willing’ ally.

keywords.name: Sunder
keywords.description: A character inflicted with Sunder has their guard reduced by X, where X is the Sunder value.

keywords.name: Sure Hit
keywords.description: Sure hit attacks always hit and do not require an accuracy roll, but they automatically miss against targets with full cover.

keywords.name: Teleport
keywords.description: You teleport instead of moving normally. Teleportation does not provoke Attacks of Opportunity and ignores most forms of slows, roots and grapples. You need to see where you teleport to, but can otherwise ignore difficult terrain and solid objects in the way. Unless stated otherwise, you only move yourself and your belongings when teleporting, not other creatures you might be touching.

keywords.name: Toxic
keywords.description: A character suffering from Toxic takes 1d6 Full Pierce Poison damage at the start of their turn.

keywords.name: Transformation
keywords.description: You can only have one transformation effect active at one time.

keywords.name: Trick Attack
keywords.description: The target of the attack must spend double RP to react to a Trick Attack.

keywords.name: Type
keywords.description: You can only be 1 ‘type’ at the same time.

keywords.name: Unarmed Strike
keywords.description: This ability must be made with an unarmed attack.

keywords.name: Unbalanced
keywords.description: Your next attack that costs AP (even 0 AP) costs 1 extra AP.

keywords.name: Upkeep
keywords.description:
You may choose to pay the cost at the beginning of your turn. If you don't, the effect is terminated.

While downed, you cannot pay upkeep.

keywords.name: Weakened
keywords.description: Your maximum AP goes down to 2 and maximum RP goes down to 1. When it ends, you regain any unused RP lost from this effect.

breakthroughs.name: 8 Eyes (Spiderfolk)
breakthroughs.description: You may have up to 8 Mystic Eyes instead of the regular 2.

breakthroughs.name: Angelblooded (Human) (Restricted)
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a human and only a human. Requires GM Approval
breakthroughs.description: You have the blood of angels in you. You may purchase the Angelblooded class.

breakthroughs.name: Arachne (Spiderfolk)
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a spiderfolk. Can only be taken at character creation.
breakthroughs.description:
You lose your extra arms racial ability. In exchange, you become Large size and your max burden is increased by 2. When attempting to move through 5ft wide spaces, it is considered difficult terrain for you and many humanoid buildings will struggle to accommodate you. You also suffer a -10 penalty to swimming checks, but you may climb through your spider climb ability at your normal speed instead of half speed.

In addition, you count as mounted for the purposes of abilities that require you to be mounted. This does not let you be a mount to other creatures.

breakthroughs.name: Become Fire (Salamander)
breakthroughs.description: The RP cost of Consume Fire is reduced to 0.

breakthroughs.name: Become Ice (Yuki-Onna)
breakthroughs.description: The RP cost of Absorb Ice is reduced to 0 the first time you use it per round. Cost is reset back to 0 when it becomes your turn

breakthroughs.name: Become Lightning (Raijin)
breakthroughs.description: The RP cost of Consume Lightning is reduced to 0 the first time you use it per round. Cost is reset back to 0 when it becomes your turn. Any Power bonus you gain from using Consume Lightning does not stack.

breakthroughs.name: Become Wind (Sylph)
breakthroughs.description: The RP cost of Consume Wind is reduced to 0 the first time you use it per round. Cost is reset back to 0 when it becomes your turn

breakthroughs.name: Blend In (Slimefolk)
breakthroughs.description:
You disguise your appearance using magic to be that of another race (and gain a +30 bonus to hide this magical effect from things such as sense magic). This skill does not allow you to change your appearance at will, but instead lets you appear as you would as a different race.  You choose this race when this breakthrough is picked up and cannot change it.

In addition, the first time you use Slime Body while disguised in this way, it costs 0 RP instead of 1 RP but reveals your actual race.  This effect does not work if the attacker knows that you are a Slimefolk.

breakthroughs.name: Blend In II (Slimefolk)
breakthroughs.description: You may disguise as a different race in addition to your chosen race during Blend In. You may take this breakthrough multiple times, selecting a new race to disguise as each time.

breakthroughs.name: Blessed by Kari (Human)
breakthroughs.description: After using Divine Providence you may use it a second time before resting, but the cost increases to 1 RP. This second use must pick a different option then your first one.

breakthroughs.name: Bully
breakthroughs.description: You gain a +5 bonus to intimidation skill checks against targets with less Fitness than you.

breakthroughs.name: Celestial Dragon (Ryujin)
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a Ryujin. Can only be taken at character creation.
breakthroughs.description: Your elemental mastery from your Ryujin's Mastery may be Holy or Dark as well. In addition, you can use Flight.

breakthroughs.name: Combat Doggy (Cu Sith)
breakthroughs.description:
You may use abilities like normal while in Dog Form and may use One-Handed weapon. Any abilities that require a specific armor or other specific physical requirements still cannot be used.

Your Dog Form no longer breaks upon taking damage.

breakthroughs.name: Combat Kitty (Cait Sith)
breakthroughs.description:
You may use abilities like normal while in cat form and may use One-Handed weapon. Any abilities that require a specific armor or other specific physical requirements still cannot be used.

Your cat form no longer breaks on damage.

breakthroughs.name: Curse of Vampirism
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be taken at character creation or after being killed by a vampire's bite.
breakthroughs.description:
You rise as a vampire, an immortal creature that feeds on the blood of living creatures and immediately gain the Vampire racial style class and its key ability. Your race changes to ‘Vampire’, but you keep the benefits of your previous race.

As a vampire, you no longer age and your physical appearance changes slightly. Your skin becomes more pale and you grow a pair of fangs. You still need to eat, drink and breathe as normal.

A vampire’s spirit core is cracked, making it difficult for it to regenerate mana naturally and requiring it to obtain it from other creatures. You no longer regenerate mana from eating (including potions), resting and can no longer use the Draw Mana encounter conclusion action. You still recover full mana at the start of a new arc. 

You are weak to sunlight. Every round you spend in sunlight without proper protection you take 10 true damage and your maximum HP is lowered by 10. Your maximum HP remains lowered until you finish a rest. You may carry a parasol or similar object in one hand to protect yourself from the sun and can do so even in combat.

In addition to these drawbacks, you no longer receive Wounds unless the damage that reduced your HP to 0 was fire, holy or true damage. You also gain 60ft Darkvision. Darkvision lets you see in total darkness, even if there's no source of light.

breakthroughs.name: Deep Connection
breakthroughs.description: You may command your mount to move and attack even if you're not mounted on it. This still using AP, Mana etc like normal as if you were mounted.

breakthroughs.name: Deus Ex Machina
breakthroughs.description: The first time you would die from a mortal wound at Encounter Conclusion, the mortal wound is removed and you instead receive a normal injury. The benefit of this breakthrough is then lost and you may not choose this breakthrough again after.

breakthroughs.name: Divine Luck I
breakthroughs.description: Once per rest, you may roll an additional dice when making a check and take the higher result.

breakthroughs.name: Divine Luck II
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have purchased Divine Luck I.
breakthroughs.description: Once per arc, you may choose to automatically succeed on a check (if success is possible).

breakthroughs.name: Divine's Chosen
breakthroughs.description:
You select one of the divines from the below list to worship. Once chosen, you can only change this decision with GM approval after a significant enough change.

Any abilities with the Divine keyword deal your chosen divine's damage instead of their listed type. 

Kari: (Type Holy) goddess of Light, the most prominent deity in the setting, almost all religious people follow Kari and it's the only serious religion with any support outside of Kirara. 

Heira: (Type Astra) goddess of Evil, mostly followed by cultists. 

Pandora: (Type Arcane) goddess of Magic (Arcane). There are a few broken-down shrines to her, not widely followed, but a few followers. 

Makai: (Type Water) goddess of the Ocean. Mostly followed in Houkaina and Kirara, moreso in Houkaina. Main temple is in Houkaina (in Northi), followed by Merfolk. 

Ayuzi Kirara: (Type Fire) goddess of Artisans. The most popular Divine in Kirara. 

Eisen: (Type Slashing) god of War. Mostly followed by goblins and orcs in Eisenstadt. Mostly seen as ceremonial and "old ways," not taken as seriously in Eisenstadt. 

Athena: (Type Lightning) goddess of Wind. Mostly followed by citizens of the area around Marlone Bay. A goddess with a quiet disposition. Mostly the "old ways," a sailor might make a gesture to Athena before setting out while not fully being a follower. 

Clio: (Type Arcane) goddess of Storytelling. Not officially followed anywhere, or even known about. Clio draws power from all of the stories forged through life, both true and fictional. 

Yggdrasil: (Type Earth) the world itself. Mostly followed by Fae in Easter. "Nature," "Terra itself" are Yggdrasil. "The will of the world/nature." Not actually a "sentient" force, but a force that creates balance and opposes destruction of natural order. Yggdrasil's strength is that it has four "superpaladins" (thaumaturges) that are bound to the world and cannot be permanently killed. The thaumaturges do not work together, and may not even be aware of each other, and may not even be aware of their mission.

breakthroughs.name: Drag along (Lamia)
breakthroughs.description:
When you have a target under the effect of "Just a hug", you can still move at half of your normal movement speed while under the Just a hug root effect and you still count as rooted for all other purposes.

When moving, you can drag along the target of Just a hug, but they still count as rooted at your new location.

In addition, your grapple power increases by +1.

breakthroughs.name: Dual Personality
breakthroughs.description:
Whether through magical or non-magical means, you have more than a single personality or entity within you through either physical or magical means. When under the influence of a Charm, Illusion or other mind-influencing effect you may spend 1 AP to switch personalities/entities and act as normal.

You may only do this once per encounter.

breakthroughs.name: Early Ascension
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be taken at character creation.
breakthroughs.description: You are treated as having 1 class mastered for the purposes of selecting a tier 2 class that has “Any class mastered” or similar requirement. This does not apply to any class that requires a specific class to be mastered and it doesn't automatically qualify you for other requirements such as weapon proficiencies.

breakthroughs.name: Elemental Affinity
breakthroughs.description:
You gain Elemental Mastery in an element of your choice.

You may pick this breakthrough more than once, choosing a different element each time.

breakthroughs.name: Elemental Breath (Ryujin)
breakthroughs.description: You may let your Dragon Breath do the damage of any element that you have mastered.

breakthroughs.name: Elixir Addict
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have used at least 3 elixirs in the same encounter.
breakthroughs.description:
You have become used to the effects of drinking elixirs, too used in fact. At the end of your turn in combat, if you do not have an Elixir active you take 6 true damage. The HP cost of drinking all elixirs is reduced by 11.

This breakthrough may be removed during an interlude phase by spending 1 IP.

breakthroughs.name: Expert Summoner
breakthroughs.requirements: At least 1 of Summoner, Mogul, Animal Summoner or Necromancer maxed. 3000+ Spirit Core
breakthroughs.description:
When you summon during the first or second round of an encounter, you may transfer main stat points from yourself into your summon.

The maximum stat points you can imbue for all your summons combined is equal to your total main stat points (Focus, Power, Agility, Toughness) - 18. You can not lower a stat below 3 with this. When you lose stat points due to this, your related values such as mana, HP and RP have their max reduced. When lowering your agility or toughness, you also lose RP or HP equal to the respective stat lost. If your  Mana is higher than your max Mana after imbuing, it is reduced to the new max.

This transfer stays until end of encounter or until the summon you invested in dies (or is otherwise removed from combat). Your max of your stats is returned to normal, but any HP or Mana lost due to this is not refunded.

You may imbue a Heroic summon with any amount of stats from this pool. These points don't need to be a direct transfer (for example, you can lower your Agility by 2 to buff your summons Power). They increase your summons values such as HP/RP etc by the regular amount these stats give.

For grunt summons, you may imbue them with half of this max. They are still capped at max 1 RP.

breakthroughs.name: Fae Flash Acrobat (Fae)
breakthroughs.description: While using Fae Flash, you may teleport a partial distance and materialize there to redirect your teleport. In a single Fae Step, you may teleport multiple times, reappearing each time you stop, to teleport from that new position. You are still limited by your maximum teleport distance and cannot take any other actions between each teleport.

breakthroughs.name: Faerie Flash Master (Fae)
breakthroughs.description: When using your Faerie Flash ability, you may spend X additional mana to increase your teleport distance by X times your movement speed.

breakthroughs.name: Faerie-Chimera Hybrid (Race)
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be chosen at character creation. Must choose Faerie or Chimera race.
breakthroughs.description:
An extremely rare condition in which a Chimera parent and a Faerie parent produces a child with Chimera traits. The odds are said to be less than 1%.

If your main race is Chimera, you may choose a Fae subrace instead of a Chimera one. If your main race is Fae, you may choose a Chimera subrace instead of a Fae one. 

You do not get any of the base traits from the other race and keep the ones from your chosen main race. However, you do get the language from the other race (or a dialect of choosing a chimera subrace)

If you pick High Fae as your subrace, you gain Fae Flash instead of Fae Flash II.

breakthroughs.name: Fast Metabolism
breakthroughs.description: Once per arc you may eat food and gain the benefits even if you already had gotten the benefits from eating food that day.

breakthroughs.name: Fast Movement (Centaur)
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be Centaur or Arachne Spiderfolk
breakthroughs.description: Your base movement speed increases by 5ft.

breakthroughs.name: Fearless
breakthroughs.description: Whenever you are afflicted by a Fear type condition, you may spend 1 RP or 0 AP to remove it.

breakthroughs.name: Fight and Flight (Chimera)
breakthroughs.description: When using Fight or Flight, you no longer receive the drawback.

breakthroughs.name: Flesheater (Jiangshi)
breakthroughs.description: When using Consume Enemy, you may consider that your food for the day and regain mana equal to a normal ration. You cannot gain this benefit if you already regained mana from food that day and using this benefit prevents you from regaining mana from food until you’ve rested.

breakthroughs.name: Flying Counter (Kitsune)
breakthroughs.description: When using Fading Counter, you may move up to your movement speed instead of 5ft. This movement has Flight and still does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

breakthroughs.name: Four Paw Sprint (Catfolk)
breakthroughs.description: When spending at least 3 AP of movement, your base movement speed is increased to 40ft instead of 25.

breakthroughs.name: Greatshield Training
breakthroughs.requirements: You must be proficient with shields.
breakthroughs.description: You gain proficiency with Greatshields.

breakthroughs.name: Heavy Armor Training
breakthroughs.requirements: You must be proficient with Light and Medium armor.
breakthroughs.description: You gain proficiency with Heavy Armor.

breakthroughs.name: Hide Behind Ally (Pixie)
breakthroughs.description: When occupying the same space as a conscious ally that's at least a size bigger than you, you may choose to become untargetable to single target attacks. The ally must be willing to take the hits for you, though they may react to these attacks as normal. While occupying the same space as a conscious ally, any effect that triggers upon not being targeted by an enemy (such as Challenge) will not be triggered. Does not work against Attacks of Opportunity.

breakthroughs.name: Human-Chimera Hybrid (Race)
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be chosen at character creation. Must choose Human race.
breakthroughs.description:
While most unions of Human and Chimera parents result in the offspring being fully of Human or fully of Chimera, there are rare instances in which the Chimera traits are still present in a human offspring.

Choose one Chimera Subrace and gain all of its features. You do not gain any of the Chimera base traits and instead have the Human ones, including Divine Providence. You do not get the 100 extra exp that humans normally get or human adaptability.

breakthroughs.name: Improved Demonic Divine Release (Demon)
breakthroughs.description:
When activating your divine release you may choose to reduce your max HP by 22. When you do, you do not pay any additional HP cost to activate it and the HP Upkeep is reduced to 0 while above 0 HP.

When you fall below 0 HP, you pay the increased Upkeep cost as normal.

breakthroughs.name: In Sync (Youkai)
breakthroughs.description:
After you use Spiritual Sync, you may cancel the effect for 0 RP at any time. If you do, you regain mana like it is described in the ability or 8 HP for each temporary mana you still had remaining.

In addition, the maximum mana or HP you can spend on Spiritual Sync is doubled.

breakthroughs.name: Kit Expert
breakthroughs.description: You may reduce the Burden cost of a single kit in your inventory by 2.

breakthroughs.name: Language Training
breakthroughs.description:
You learn a language of your choice. Rare, dead or similar languages may be unavailable (GM’s discretion).

You may take this breakthrough multiple times, picking a different language each time.

breakthroughs.name: Large Specimen (Nio, Bullfolk or Bearfolk)
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a Nio, Bullfolk or Bearfolk.
breakthroughs.description: Your size becomes Large.

breakthroughs.name: Light Armor Training
breakthroughs.description: You gain proficiency with Light Armor and shields.

breakthroughs.name: Light Sleeper
breakthroughs.description: When asleep, you may roll Perception rolls as if you were awake to be aware of danger approaching.

breakthroughs.name: Mark of Conflict
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be an Unknown Paladin that follows Eisen. Must have the Mark of Justice ability.
breakthroughs.description:
The effect of your Mark of Justice changes to the following:

“You mark a single enemy, inflicting the Mark of Conflict on them. If an enemy moves away from you and not towards another ally, they take Full Pierce physical damage equal to your Power for each 20ft of movement they spent moving away from you.”

The range and AP cost remain the same.

breakthroughs.name: Medium Armor Training
breakthroughs.requirements: You must be proficient with Light Armor
breakthroughs.description: You gain proficiency with Medium Armor.

breakthroughs.name: Mental Torture (Unseelie)
breakthroughs.description: When you roll a natural 20 on your accuracy roll, you may apply the effects of Torture Techniques even if the enemy Dodges or Blocks it.

breakthroughs.name: Mixed House (Demon)
breakthroughs.description: You choose another house to gain the benefit of.

breakthroughs.name: Mystic Eyes of Faerie Light (Fae)
breakthroughs.description:
Your Fae eyes have developed into the Eyes of Faerie Light.  You may purchase the Faerie Light Eyes class.

In addition, you can make a Perception check at +10 bonus to determine if something is an illusion. You are not immune to these illusions however.

breakthroughs.name: Natural Immunity (Ratfolk)
breakthroughs.description: When you successfully resist the effect of a disease or poison (or are immune to the effect), you may choose to become afflicted anyway. You suffer no effects from a disease or poison you choose to accept this way. This poison or disease lasts the normal duration or until the end of the encounter, whichever is shorter.

breakthroughs.name: On the draw
breakthroughs.description: You gain +1 to your initiative.

breakthroughs.name: Organized Inventory
breakthroughs.description: Increases your in-combat burden capacity by 1.

breakthroughs.name: Organized Inventory II
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have the Organized Inventory breakthrough
breakthroughs.description: Your in-combat Burden capacity is increased by 1.

breakthroughs.name: Organized Inventory III
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have the Organized Inventory II breakthrough
breakthroughs.description: Your in-combat Burden capacity is increased by 1.

breakthroughs.name: Overrun (Centaur)
breakthroughs.description: When using the Charge or Spear Charge ability your movement speed is increased by 5ft and if your attack made through the Charge ability does damage, it knocks the target prone.

breakthroughs.name: Panda Martial Arts (Red Panda)
breakthroughs.description:
You can be in Panda stance at the same time as another stance without either stance ending.

Other rules for stance breaking (such as entering 2 non-panda stances) still apply.

breakthroughs.name: Photosynthesis (Dryad)
breakthroughs.description: By spending at least an hour in the direct sunlight, you may gain the benefits of having eaten food and you do not need to eat or drink for the next 24 hours.

breakthroughs.name: Power Saving Mode (Ancient Marionette)
breakthroughs.description: If you are at maximum mana during your meal, you only need to consume half the normal amount to be well fed.

breakthroughs.name: Powerful Ki (Oni)
breakthroughs.description: When using Gravitational Ki, the range increases by 30ft. The push and pull distance increases by up to 10ft. In addition, you may spend 1 AP instead of 1 RP on it.

breakthroughs.name: Primary Stat Training
breakthroughs.description:
You gain a +1 bonus to Focus, Power, Agility or Toughness.

This breakthrough can be selected multiple times. The effects stack. Each time you take this breakthrough the cost increases by 100, up to a maximum of 700.

breakthroughs.name: Racial Flight
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be Phoenix, Mothfolk, Lizardfolk, Sylph or Willowisp race.
breakthroughs.description: You may use Flight.

breakthroughs.name: Rapid Flash (High Fae)
breakthroughs.description: Your Fae Flash gains the Rapid keyword.

breakthroughs.name: Rich Parents
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be taken at character creation.
breakthroughs.description: You start the game with an additional 3000 Clim of funds.

breakthroughs.name: Secondary Stat Training
breakthroughs.description:
You gain a +1 bonus to Fitness, Cunning, Reason, Awareness or Presence.

This breakthrough can be selected multiple times. The effects stack.

breakthroughs.name: Skill Training
breakthroughs.description:
You gain a single skill point or two expertise points to spend on a skill. Crafting skills cannot be selected with this training.

You may select this breakthrough multiple times. Its effects can stack.

breakthroughs.name: Skilled Flier
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have Flight racial ability or Racial Flight breakthrough
breakthroughs.description:
When you are about to lose Height from taking damage due to your Flight ability, you may instead spend 3 Mana to negate losing height from the flight mechanic until the start of your next turn.

Abilities that make you lose height not part of the Flight ability (such as downburst) may still knock you out of the air.

breakthroughs.name: Slime Summoner
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a mastered Animal Summoner.
breakthroughs.description:
When using the Summon Animal ability, you may instead choose to summon slimes. You roll randomly from the following slimes: Slime, Fire Slime, Earth Slime, Water Slime, Wind Slime or Mana Slime.

Even if you have the Wildheart class, you still cannot choose which slime you summon except you may choose to summon the regular Slime.

breakthroughs.name: Slow Starter
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be taken at character creation.
breakthroughs.description: You receive 200 less EXP at character creation to spend on classes and abilities. Every time you get EXP after character creation, you get twice as much. This lasts until you’ve received a total of 500 (1000 when doubled) exp.

breakthroughs.name: Small Doggy (Cu Sith)
breakthroughs.description: When you enter your Dog Form, you become a small dog instead. Instead of the usual bonuses and penalties, you instead lose 4 guard and 8 Block but gain a +2 Size bonus to Evasion and Dodge.

breakthroughs.name: Small Specimen (Cowfolk)
breakthroughs.requirements: Cowfolk only. Must be taken at character creation.
breakthroughs.description: Your size is Small instead of Medium.

breakthroughs.name: Speciality Weapon Training
breakthroughs.description:
You gain proficiency with a Speciality Weapon group.

This breakthrough can be selected multiple times. You must select a different weapon group each time you select it.

breakthroughs.name: Summon Contract: Fortuna, Lady Luck
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a summoner and have visited the eidolon.
breakthroughs.description:
Appearance: Fortuna appears as a beautiful lady wearing clothing of the highest quality. Her clothes change each time she appears, but she always carries with her a parasol designed like a roulette wheel.
Desires: Fortuna desires to see gambling. To have people bet their all on impossible odds.
Pact Cost: You can never naturally roll 20 again. Every 20 you roll is reduced to 19.
Attunement Cost: None
Re-Summon Cost: Roll a natural 20 (before the pact cost reduces it) on an attack or skill check with consequences for failure (GM’s decision).

When you contract Fortuna, you are able to attune to it. While attuned, you gain access to the Draw Luck ability through your Channel Eidolon ability. You summon the Jack of Hearts for your Lesser Eidolon and Fortuna for your Eidolon (The stats for these are listed under monsters).

breakthroughs.name: Summon Contract: Ixilune, The Swarm
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a summoner and have visited the eidolon.
breakthroughs.description:
Appearance: Hot bug lady.
Desires: Ixilune desires to consume everything.
Pact Cost: You need to eat 1.5x as much food to be fed.
Attunement Cost: None
Re-Summon Cost: Must eat the flesh of a creature of the same (main) race.

When you contract Ixilune, you are able to attune to it. While attuned, you gain access the Distracting Swarm ability through your Channel Eidolon ability. You summon the Devouring Swarm for your Lesser Eidolon and Ixilune for your Eidolon. (The stats for these are listed under monsters.)

breakthroughs.name: Summon Contract: Pipoltr, The Gardener
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be a summoner and have visited the eidolon.
breakthroughs.description:
• Appearance: Pipoltr appears as a giant scarab beetle whose carapace glints with a metallic sheen like burnished bronze and emerald green.  His presence is both otherworldly and ancient, curved antennae sprout from his head that can detect the health of plants.  His compound eyes shine like brilliant gems.
  • Desires: Pipoltr’s desire is the health of nature.
  • Pact Cost:  1 Maximum Mana.
  • Attunement Cost: None
  • Re-Summon Eidolon:  Character must spend an EP to perform 1 day of gardening work before resummoning Pipoltr.

When you contract Pipoltr, you are able to attune to it. While attuned, you gain access the Vine Wall Cover ability through your Channel Eidolon ability. You summon the Rhinoceros Beetle for your Lesser Eidolon and Pipoltr for your Eidolon. (The stats for these are listed under monsters.)

breakthroughs.name: Superior Escapist (Rabbitfolk)
breakthroughs.description: You may use your Escape Artist when Rooted to remove it in addition to grapples.

breakthroughs.name: Tengu Defensive Aura (Tengu)
breakthroughs.description: Your resistance to astra corruption is increased by 1 (Your SC is treated as 500 higher when determining if you suffer from astra corruption). In addition, you do not suffer any negative effects when the astra level is raised artificially. (such as from Exousiai's).

breakthroughs.name: The Unknown Paladin
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have the Divine's Chosen breakthrough.
breakthroughs.description:
Despite not being human, you fulfill the human requirement to become a Paladin. In addition, your Smite skill's damage type changes to one that represents your chosen Divine. The paladin holy weapon key ability also changes its damage type to the one that represents your chosen Divine.

Kari: Holy 
Heira: Astra
Pandora: Arcane
Makai: Water
Ayuzi Kirara: Fire 
Eisen: Physical 
Athena: Lightning 
Clio: Arcane 
Yggdrasil: Earth

breakthroughs.name: Third Eye
breakthroughs.description: You may have up to 3 Mystic Eyes instead of the regular 2.

breakthroughs.name: Touched by Death
breakthroughs.requirements: Must be taken at character creation or after your HP has dropped below 0 in an encounter.
breakthroughs.description:
Near-death experiences sometimes leave people more sensitive to death itself, manifesting in what is called the Shinigami’s Eyes. You may purchase the Shinigami Eyes class.

In addition, you may spend 1 AP to see the HP percentage and weak spots (if any) of all creatures for 1 turn.

breakthroughs.name: Universal Training
breakthroughs.description:
You gain +1 to any primary stat, +1 to any secondary stat and 5 skill points. You may put these skill points into any normal skill, except crafting and gathering skills.

This breakthrough may be taken multiple times. The effects stack.

breakthroughs.name: Weapon Training
breakthroughs.description:
You gain proficiency with a weapon group. You may not select Speciality Weapons with this.

This breakthrough can be selected multiple times. You must select a different weapon group each time you select it.

breakthroughs.name: Wide Circuits I
breakthroughs.description: Your maximum mana increases by 1.

breakthroughs.name: Wide Circuits II
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have the Wide Circuits breakthrough.
breakthroughs.description: Your maximum Mana is increased by 1.

breakthroughs.name: Wide Circuits III
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have the Wide Circuits II breakthrough.
breakthroughs.description: Your maximum Mana is increased by 1.

breakthroughs.name: Wide Circuits IV
breakthroughs.requirements: Must have the Wide Circuits III breakthrough
breakthroughs.description:
Your maximum Mana is increased by 1.

You may take this breakthrough multiple times. The effects stack.

monsters.name: Acolyte
monsters.strategy: Acolytes serve as frontliners that can heal themselves or allies. Cure Touch can be used immediately when an ally drops low enough to gain the full benefit from it. Acolytes should prioritize healing heroic allies over grunt allies.
monsters.runningMonster:
Acolytes are intended to be a base for generic grunt enemies that focus on being a healer. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Priest’ generic enemy.

Acolytes can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Acolytes can use either a channeling weapon or a light melee weapon + shield. Acolytes can wear anything from no armor, light armor to medium armor. In the stat block, a light melee weapon + shield and light armor is assumed.
monsters.appearance: Varies
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Acolytes are beginning spellcasters that draw their power from the gods. Due to the popularity and strength of Kari, the human goddess, the vast majority of acolyte’s in the world are human. However, acolytes of other races do still exist. Some may follow Kari, while others may follow their own god or goddess.

monsters.name: Alchemic Golem
monsters.strategy:
The Alchemic Golem is a powerhouse able to take on an entire party on its own.  With its high action economy and its ability to mitigate damage every turn it can create a significant challenge for any party.  

You'll want to run the Alchemic Golem in an enclosed space where it can utilize Transmute Low Wall to force players (especially ranged ones) to waste AP on movement.  By using the wall to create a small "pool" you can then flood the pool with Alchemic Flare to prep it for next turn.  Make sure you tell players that are within the pool that they can smell gas to foreshadow the attack.  On the next turn you can use Alchemic Flare to punish any players within the pool, forcing them to abide by your mechanics.

The Alchemic Golem is a beast in close range too.  Move into melee range and deliver all of your AP in light and heavy attacks of your choice and then fire Transmutation Cannon to knock them away.  You can create a more mechanical fight by utilizing enemy positionings and walls to maximize Transmutation Cannon's damage.

Zero Impact Generator should be used anytime damage is taken by the Golem or any of its other body parts.

Alchemic Barrage is a ticking timer, that forces the party to press the attack by whittling down their RP or HP.  Once the Golem is below 50% health it unlocks Alchemic Barrage II, which allows you to focus down a player who is low RP, or force them into taking cover.

Once at half health, Alchemic Golem engages Overdrive which grants it +2 extra AP, further increasing the pressure.

You want to encourage the players to be creative and attack the specific bodyparts to reduce the Golem's action economy.  Make sure you emphasize which body part is doing which attack and that the Zero Impact Generator only protects other bodyparts.  The Golem itself has incredibly high HP, so its worth it for the party to attack those parts.  If they aren't getting the picture, try some forced skill checks to realize what is going on, or even use a NPC companion to attack the bodyparts while showcasing the effectiveness of it.

If the party attacks any body part that doesn't have a special effect, just have the damage translate to the body, but also make sure to let them know it seems to have little effect.  Once one of the bodyparts reaches 0 HP, it is destroyed and its linked actions are no longer available.
monsters.runningMonster:
Alchemic Golem is a great end of arc boss, providing a high amount of danger.  It can face a party by itself with its high action economy and can be mixed with other creatures to face off against higher level enemies.

The main body of the Golem should be at least 20ft x 20ft.

You'll also want to run this enemy in an enclosed space with a small amount of key line of sight cover.  A space around 120ft x 70ft with walls on all sides is recommended.  If you would like to do a larger space, make sure that you increase the width of Transmute Low Wall to match, but big open fields are not recommended for this enemy.
monsters.appearance: x
monsters.habitat: x
monsters.lore:
Alchemic Golems are formidable constructs meticulously crafted by skilled Artificers and Alchemists. These hulking guardians come in various configurations, each tailored to serve specific security purposes within their designated domains. Typically stationed as protectors, Alchemic Golems stand sentinel over valuable treasures, ancient secrets, and critical research facilities, ensuring that only those deemed worthy may pass.

Despite their imposing size and intricate designs, each Golem exhibits a unique blend of alchemical prowess and mechanical ingenuity, reflecting the expertise of their creators. Adventurers delving into forgotten ruins or exploring cutting-edge research facilities can expect to encounter diverse variants of these sentinels. Whether guarding the remnants of a lost civilization or the forefront of arcane experimentation, Alchemic Golems present both a significant challenge and a testament to the enduring legacy of their makers.

monsters.name: Alpha Wolf
monsters.strategy: If not engaged in melee, the alpha wolf will move up to the most vulnerable target it can reach without provoking attacks of opportunity. It will use Leading Bite against the target if it can get wolves in range with it. If an enemy is prone, it will use Go for the throat.
monsters.runningMonster:
An alpha wolf should be ran with several normal wolves to provide a good challenge for a group of adventurers. An alpha wolf cannot do much by itself and absolutely needs normal wolves around to function as an enemy.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Direhide (alpha wolf pelt)
monsters.appearance: A big wolf, larger than a normal one.
monsters.habitat: Usually found in a forest.
monsters.lore: A big wolf in charge of a pack.

monsters.name: Amanita Mushroom
monsters.strategy: The Amanita mushroom runs up to the closest target it can see and attacks it normally. Upon taking damage, it will use Poison Spore.
monsters.runningMonster:
A dozen or so Amanita Mushrooms can make a threatening encounter for the average group of adventurers. They become more dangerous when the player’s movement is restricted, either through the size of the room or by the mushrooms surrounding the party.

Gather Parts: 250 Alchemy units
monsters.appearance: A large mushroom with a spotted red cap. Looks similar to the normal mushroom, but with a size that of a regular person. It also has a face on the stalk, along with a pair of arms and legs attached to it.
monsters.habitat: Found in damp, dark places.
monsters.lore: An almost mindless creature, the Amanita will attack nearby people if it needs to feed. Otherwise, it is docile unless provoked.

monsters.name: Animal Summoner
monsters.strategy:
The summoner spends the first action of its turn casting Summon Beast. After that, it will use Empower Beast if none of the animals are currently empowered. If there is an empowered one, it will use Bestial Command on that creature, assuming the creature is able to attack.

If the summoner is attacked, it will most likely use the animal shield ability to redirect the attack unless the summoner is high on HP/RP and the attack would kill the animal.
monsters.runningMonster: The summoner can be run together with another heroic ally. If it is the sole heroic enemy, it should start with several grunt type animals already presummoned.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: The process of animal summoning is usually done by Fae, but any mage can learn it if they are in tune with nature.

monsters.name: Apprentice
monsters.strategy: Apprentices prefer to stay in the back, using Glittershards to block off enemy ranged attackers. After that, they will start to cast Missile Barrage until their mana runs out. If engaged in melee, will disengage and attempt to move away.
monsters.runningMonster:
Apprentices are intended to be a base for generic grunt enemies that focus on being both a ranged controller and AoE striker. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Mage’ generic enemy.

Apprentices can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Apprentices generally use a channeling weapon and wear no armor.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Apprentices are beginning spellcasters without a specialization. They exist in every race, though human mages are the rarest ones.

monsters.name: Archer
monsters.strategy: The archer's strategy in combat is to sit still as far away as possible and do damage to the most vulnerable target, usually a spellcaster not in cover. When engaged in melee, they will swap to a melee weapon if they have one.
monsters.runningMonster:
Archers are intended to be generic grunt enemies that focus on ranged combat. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Sniper’ generic enemy.

Archers can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Archers can use any type of ranged weapon, though pistols, shotguns and sniper rifles are rarely seen. Archers often wear no or light armor. Most will also carry a light melee weapon as a backup weapon.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Archer is a name given to all users of ranged weaponry, regardless of whether they use a bow or not. They exist in every race and can use a wide variety of ranged weapons.

monsters.name: Armored Spider
monsters.strategy:
The armored spider will move up and attacks the nearest enemy target, using Poison Bite whenever it can.

If it gets targeted by an attack it will use Defensive Curl, then use Block every time it can while the stance lasts.
monsters.runningMonster: The armored spider should be run in combination with other types of spiders.
monsters.appearance: A large spider covered in a thick carapace.
monsters.habitat: The armored spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.
monsters.lore: A type of large spider that has evolved into having a thick armored carapace, giving it more bulk than other spider species.

monsters.name: Assassin
monsters.strategy: Assassins aim for the backline, targeting enemy mages or archers. They aim to creep up while stealthed, then go in for a backstab. Once they’re on a target, they will keep attacking that target, using Evasive Maneuver aggressively if needed. If they get swarmed, they will use the disengage action and retreat to wait for a better opportunity to strike again.
monsters.strongAgainst: Parties with low perception, Low defense parties
monsters.runningMonster:
Assassins are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on skirmishing. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Rogue’ generic enemy.

An assassin can be run as a threat alongside several grunts, as a small group of 2-3 assassins or in a balanced group of heroic enemies combining it with others of its type like the Defender, Sniper etc.

Assassins prefer light or no armor along with a pair of light weapons, usually daggers.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: While the original assassins come from the desert city of Telsin, the term has evolved since then. It now refers to any sort of stealthy individual who seeks to eliminate priority targets quickly and efficiently. They exist in the employ of all major nations in the world, and people with a similar skill set are not hard to find in adventurer’s guilds, as well as other organizations.

monsters.name: Astral Spider
monsters.strategy: The Astral Spider will start hidden and remain hidden until an enemy has moved the range of its blink. When that happens, it will Blink onto that target, choosing the least armored one if multiple targets are available, and attack it. After that, it will use Poison Bite each time it can.
monsters.runningMonster: The astral spiders should be run with several other of the grunt spiders. Don't run too many at the same time, as an ambush from many blinks at the same time can easily leave a character dead.
monsters.appearance: A large spider whose form seems almost transparent.
monsters.habitat: The astral spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.
monsters.lore: A type of large spiders that has suffered from astral corruption, giving it teleportation abilities.

monsters.name: Astral Tiger
monsters.strategy: An astral tiger’s main strategy is to use Desync to reposition out of range of their melee attackers or to approach ranged attackers. They will prioritize jumping on people with low HP or RP to hit them with their Resync Bite.
monsters.runningMonster:
Three to four astral tigers is decent challenge for a group of adventurers.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Astra Tiger Pelt
monsters.appearance: A translucent tiger.
monsters.habitat: Usually found close to the astra line. Rarely found in places that have normal tigers.
monsters.lore: The astral tiger is a tiger that has been corrupted by Astra. It phases in and out of reality at seeming random times, though the beast itself always seem perfectly aware of how it will move.

monsters.name: Astran Magpie
monsters.strategy: The astran magpie follows the targeting order described in its Strike of the Shiny ability. It will use Swooping Strike exclusively.
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of astran magpies + 1 or 2 greater astran magpie's make a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Due to the tendency to go for shiny armored targets, they can be a lot less scary if the group has a heavy tank and no person wearing valuables.

Gather Parts: 50u of feathersteel from their talons.
monsters.appearance: Two eyes on each side of its head (four total) otherwise looks like a larger magpie.
monsters.habitat: The astra line.
monsters.lore:
An astra corrupted magpie.

By Mega Mike 70

monsters.name: Bandersnatch
monsters.strategy:
The bandersnatch starts with Dire Claw at the start of its turn. If it cannot reach any enemies without moving or if it can finish off an injured target, it will use Mana Razor Alpha.

The rest of its abilities are used immediately when they become available.
monsters.runningMonster:
A single bandersnatch is a challenging encounter for a party.

Gather Parts: 2 claws, each containing 2000 units of mithril. Can be gathered from twice, once for each claw.
monsters.appearance: A bipedal furry monster with massive Mithril claws.
monsters.habitat: The heartwood in the astra line
monsters.lore: Angry furry cat

monsters.name: Bear
monsters.strategy: The bear attacks the nearest target with Maul and light attacks
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of bears is required for them to be a serious threat to a group of adventurers.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides or food units (meat).
monsters.appearance: A large bear.
monsters.habitat: Found in the forest in many places.
monsters.lore: A common bear. Not a threat to adventurers, but still dangerous to the average person.

monsters.name: Black Knight
monsters.strategy:
The black knight will use Black Knight's Charge whenever it can target someone more than 20ft away. If it is surrounded by 2 or more enemies, it will use Sweep. It will also use sweep if it allows the use of the charge. After using their Black Knight's Charge, it will always use Impale if it can.

Finally, if it ever gets dismounted it will use its Esoteric Art: All Out. It makes blocking useless, but it can still dodge.
monsters.runningMonster: A single Black Knight will provide a challenge for an adventuring party. Like all mounted enemies, it will shine in open spaces and struggle in enclosed spaces.
monsters.appearance: An ominous figure clad in heavy black armor that rides on top of a steed made out of shadows.
monsters.habitat: Found in the astra line.
monsters.lore: To do.

monsters.name: Boar
monsters.strategy: The boar will use Goring Charge if possible and there’s no enemy in range. Else it will simply attack or move closer to attack.
monsters.runningMonster:
Boars need to be a large pack, 10+ to pose a challenge to a group of adventurer’s. A boar can serve as a pet to a heroic unit. Boars are strongest when they fight in an open field where their charge will leave them out of range of counterattacks. In terrain with many obstacles, they may find themselves caught without much to do.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides or food units (meat).
monsters.appearance: A boar.
monsters.habitat: Can be found in many places in the wild.
monsters.lore: A common boar.

monsters.name: Broodmother
monsters.strategy:
The core part of the broodmother's strategy is the Webbing and Feast skills. The broodmother will always cast Webbing on an enemy if there are no enemies it can safely reach and attack currently inside a web. It gains Lock-on against enemies inside the web, even if they aren't rooted, so it will prioritize attacks on those enemies. It will use Poison Bite each time it can.

The feast ability has a 4 AP cost and the setup keyword, meaning that it can't immediately finish even if the broodmother has 4 AP. The smartest way to use Feast is to only use it when the broodmother has 0 AP left, this will let the broodmother get in the maximum number of attacks even if the feast attempt fails due to the target being freed from the web. However, as the GM you can use this variable cost to make the fight easier if needed.
monsters.runningMonster:
The broodmother is intended as a mostly solo fight, though against stronger groups or groups that have easy access to fire you can add in a few of the grunt spiders.

The burrowing spiders that appear from the broodmother's passive should act on initiative 0. This gives players enough time to deal with them if they play well and they don't risk getting burrowed in without being able to do anything against it.
monsters.appearance: A giant spider with a dozen of red eyes.
monsters.habitat: The broodmother lives in caves or underground, covering the tunnels with webbing.
monsters.lore: The broodmother is a giant spider that births other spiders.

monsters.name: Brute
