monsters.strategy: Brute engage the frontline in combat and hit the most vulnerable target there. If they can’t make a Heavy attack, they will use Slam if possible. If they have to get in range first, they will use Charge to do so.
monsters.runningMonster:
Brutes are intended to be a base for generic Grunt enemies that focus on being a hardhitting melee. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Warrior’ generic enemy.

Brutes can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Brutes generally use heavy melee weapons. They can use no armor, light armor or medium armor depending on the race. The stat block below assumes light armor and a 2handed melee weapon. Some might carry a ranged weapon as backup.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Brutes are combatants that specialize in melee combat. They exist in every race and civilization and can use a wide variety of weapons and armor.

monsters.name: Burrowing Spider
monsters.strategy: A burrowing spider will move up to the closest target. If it can, it will use Burrow. Once it is inside a host, it will use Dig Deeper each turn.
monsters.runningMonster: A burrowing spider is not much of a threat by itself, or even in a large group. A burrowing spider is only dangerous if its ignored, since it takes them a turn of being in melee range before they use burrow and become dangerous. Have them drop down on players or come from behind or from little nooks to allow them to get close. But always give players enough time to react to them.
monsters.appearance: A tiny spider.
monsters.habitat: The burrowing spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.
monsters.lore: A tiny spider that is like a parasite. Once it finds its way inside a host, it eats its way to the targets heart.

monsters.name: Cheetah
monsters.strategy: The cheetah rushes in with its pounce ability then fights as normal.
monsters.runningMonster:
Cheetahs are only a threat against adventurers when they appear in a group. Putting them a decent distance away from the players so they can use their pounce ability to its maximum effect can help even things out.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides or food units (meat).
monsters.appearance: A large feline with a spotted skin.
monsters.habitat: Savannah's and temperate to hot deserts.
monsters.lore: A spotted big cat.

monsters.name: Crystal Behemoth
monsters.strategy:
The crystal behemoth automatically reacts with Crystal Barrier when targeted with an attack if it can.

If it can use Crystal Burst, it will. Otherwise, it will use Crystal Stomp.

If it's close to an enemy, it will use Rock Crunching Bite and a mix of Light and Heavy attacks. If it struggles to reach an enemy, it will instead use Astra Beams spending all its AP on it. If it identifies a silver weapon threat, it will try to focus that enemy.
monsters.weakAgainst: The elemental races that absorb damage.
monsters.runningMonster:
The crystal behemoth is a suitable threat to a party. It can be defeated in two ways, either by draining its mana to 0 by letting it use crystal burst or by defeating it the normal way. The crystal burst way ensures even parties without magic users can defeat it, though they it will most likely not be a great fight for them.

Note that it will not drop a core if it kills itself with crystal burst.

Drops: Crystal Behemoth Core
monsters.appearance: A large gray fiend with purple crystals embedded into its skin.
monsters.habitat: The Corwood in the astra line.
monsters.lore: A large fiend that feeds on the purple crystals that are embedded in its skin.

monsters.name: Deathcap Mushroom
monsters.strategy: The deathcap mushroom will start the fight by using Spore Launch at the largest group of enemies it can reach. After that, it will fight normally. When it takes damage, it will use Poison Spore as a reaction.
monsters.runningMonster:
Two deathcap mushrooms or a deathcap mushroom combined with several amanita mushrooms can provide a suitable threat for a group of adventurers. A deathcap mushroom can provide a lasting debuff to a party that does not have ways to remove poison.

Gather Parts: 500 alchemy units
monsters.habitat: Found in damp, dark places.

monsters.name: Defender
monsters.strategy: The defender’s combat strategy depends a bit on who their allies are. In general, they want to stick near their vulnerable allies and force melee enemies to attack the defender instead through Threatening Aura. If someone is Challenged, they will use Raise Shield. If they ever hit an attack of opportunity, they will always follow it up with Sweeping Opportunity.
monsters.runningMonster:
Defenders are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on being a tanky frontline. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Tank’ generic enemy.

Defenders pair best with melee attackers that don’t have as much defense as they do. They can be run with a bunch of Grunt level allies or with a group of around 3 others of a similar type to them like the Assassin or Sniper etc.

The above stat block assumes they are using Medium Armor and a Shield. Any melee weapon can work for a defender, though polearms are the best option.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Defenders are front liners who go in first and absorb the hits for their allies. Existing in every culture and of any race, they are usually heavily armored with shields.

monsters.name: Devouring Swarm
monsters.lore:
Summoning Cost: 1 AP, 1 Mana

10x10ft size

monsters.name: Drake
monsters.strategy:
The drake will begin the fight by flying and attacking the party from the sky. It can use both Fireball and Flame Breath in the same turn while flying. If its mana runs out before being forced to the ground, it will land itself and attack as normal.

If the drake is forced to land through its soft wings ability, it will stay grounded unless it can take flight again without provoking attacks of opportunities. It can still use its Flame Breath even while on the ground, as long as it still has mana.
monsters.runningMonster:
A group of drakes can provide a good challenge to an adventuring party, though they might be too much to handle depending on the party composition.

Running a pair of drake as a harasser from the sky can make a fight that drains the party's resources without there being a significant risk of anyone dying.

A drake is a size bigger than the wyrmling and a normal humanoid character.

Gather Parts: 250 units of Dragonscale.
monsters.appearance: A large scaled lizard with a pair of wings on its back.
monsters.habitat: Most commonly found high in the mountain in places with a warm temperature.
monsters.lore: A distant relative of the dragons that have vanished. Though they spent most of their time sleeping in their caves, they are hostile to all living creatures and view them are little more than prey.

monsters.name: Drake Wyrmling (Fire)
monsters.strategy: The wyrmling will stay at range when it can and use its Firebolt ability to weaken the enemy. When engaged in melee, it will fight as normal.
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of wyrmlings will provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. They can also be used together with their stronger relatives like the drake and wyrm.

Gather Parts: 100 units of dragonscale.
monsters.appearance: A small scaled lizard with a pair of wings on its back.
monsters.habitat: Most commonly found high in the mountain in places with a warm temperature.
monsters.lore: A distant relative of the dragons that have vanished. The wyrmling is a young wyrm that has not yet matured. Despite their age, they are not any less hostile and vicious - attacking any unknown creature that approaches it.

monsters.name: Dreameater
monsters.strategy:
Against a single enemy, the dreameater will do a normal round of combat then do the Nightmare cage on the following round. Immediately following that with Dream Ender on the turn after.

Against a group of enemies, it will do the same thing if it wins initiative. Otherwise, it will immediately cast Nightmare Cage on the target that it was targeting while alone. Once the cage is broken, it has little else going for it and can only do basic attacks.

Should it kill a target with Dream Ender, it will keep repeating the Nightmare Cage into Dream Ender loop until all enemies are defeated.
monsters.runningMonster:
The dreameater will initially target a single player, preferably one who goes to bed early or who is separate from the rest of the party. They will wake up fighting an enemy they likely cannot defeat by themselves. Any HP or Mana they spent during this is not actually used. Afterwards, they will wake up normally and feel like they had a bad dream.

The dreameater will keep targeting the same player every night if no actions are taken.

The players must go to sleep near each other and at the same time in order to all fight it. Once they do, the dream eater will most likely be an easy kill.

If your party has less than 4 players, be sure to adjust the HP on the cage accordingly.
monsters.appearance: Varies
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: A formless creature that only ever appears in someone's dreams. It can seemingly enter the dream of anyone, no matter how far away they are. Targets people that are alone and enjoys tormenting its prey until they eventually die to exhaustion. Once it has chosen its target, it will keep visiting it until either it or the victim dies.

monsters.name: Dredge Ooze
monsters.strategy:
A melee dredge ooze will move to the nearest enemy it can reach and attack them. It will not move if it can still attack a creature.

A ranged dredge ooze will remain stationary unless it can only attack something by moving.
monsters.runningMonster:
The Dredge ooze is a creature that can snowball out of control if left unchecked. Use a lower amount of them than for a normal grunt fight, around 12 for a 4 man party. If the players have strong anti-grunt tools, you can consider adding more.

You should divide the Dredge Ooze into melee and ranged ones, and only use the ranged attack on those ranged ones. Because of their wall climb nature, you can put them on top of cliffs or hanging from the ceiling.

Gather Parts: Dredge Ooze Sludge worth 700 Clim. It's an alchemy ingredient that can be used to make [REDACTED].
monsters.appearance: A creature made from a black goo type substance.
monsters.habitat: Found in astra corrupted area's
monsters.lore: A common slime type creature corrupted by Astra. Now hostile to any living creature it sees.

monsters.name: Earth Slime
monsters.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Ghimslag flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Earth Herb.
monsters.appearance: A small cute slime.
monsters.lore:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

monsters.name: Efreet
monsters.strategy: The Efreet seeks to move up alongside their Unstable Efreet.
monsters.runningMonster: Best paired with several Unstable Efreet.

monsters.name: Faewolf
monsters.strategy:
The faewolf will start the battle in Shimmer. If it can, it will teleport to the squishiest looking enemy and attack it with a Heavy attack and Arcane Fang.

Every turn while it has mana, it will repeat those moves and use the remaining AP on movement or light attacks.
monsters.runningMonster:
A group of ~4 faewolves will provide a challenge to a party of 4.

Because of their nature as ambushers and their high mobility, be careful of how you run these. Three wolves teleporting in on anyone may very well down them. Likewise, three arcane fangs on the same target can add a lot of damage quickly. If running a high number of faewolves, skipping the stealth part may be best.

The wolves should all focus fire a target if you want to play them to be deadly, but otherwise you can also have them attack different targets.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Faewolf pelt
monsters.appearance: Faewolves are lean, lupine beasts whose fur shimmers like astral mist. Their eyes burn with a fae-like glow, a sign of their internal magical reserves.
monsters.habitat: They favor dense forests or snowy highlands close to fey rifts, where ambient magic saturates the environment. Lone Faewolves may venture farther if drawn by potent magical signatures—like adventurers bearing artifacts or high spirit cores.
monsters.lore: Legends say these wolves were once normal forest predators who stumbled upon a fey nexus or were subject to an otherworldly curse. Over generations, they’ve adapted, developing unique teleportation powers fueled by a blend of spiritual mana and wild fae energy.

monsters.name: Fire Slime
monsters.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Salachar flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Fire Herb.
monsters.appearance: A small cute slime.
monsters.lore:
Just a fire slime.

By Nya.

monsters.name: Fortuna
monsters.lore: Summon cost: 4 AP, 4 Mana

monsters.name: Frost Maiden
monsters.strategy:
The Frost Maiden is an assassin that functions by limiting the enemies vision and luring them apart from each other, then striking an isolated target. 

She will start the battle by using Blizzard. On her first turn, she will use Blizzard Walker and wait around 40ft away from the enemies. If the enemies spread out to look for her, she can move in with Snow Assassin on her next turn to attack a target, then follow it up with normal attacks after.

From that point, she can alternate Blizzard Walker and Snow Assassin to get favorable engagements with a lower amount of enemies present.
monsters.runningMonster:
A group of frost maiden provides a challenging fight for high spirit core players.

As the GM, you can wait for a turn to see if the players will spread out and stumble into the blizzard alone to look for the frost maiden after the first turn. If they don't, then the frost maiden should just attack to not waste anybody's time. Make sure to hide the token after she moves out of vision range to further tempt people to spread out. Also, remember that if the frost maiden doesn't attack on her first turn, she can use her remaining AP to move and circle around the party to further throw them off about where she is.
monsters.appearance: A beautiful woman with pale or blue skin and white hair.
monsters.habitat: Can be found in any place where it freezes for most of the year.
monsters.lore: An ice elemental type creature that is inherently attracted to the warmth of other creatures. Said to be a manifestation of travelers that got lost in a blizzard and closely related to the yuki-onna youkai. Not a creature with malicious intent necessarily, but her way of thinking may be too alien to negotiate with.

monsters.name: Gargoyle
monsters.strategy: Gargoyles will start the fight by flying over the largest group of enemies and using Stone Form. After that, they will fight normally with light and heavy attacks unless they can use Stone Form again without provoking an attack of opportunity. They may use Stone Form even when on the ground if they are isolated and about to take many hits, especially if already low on RP.
monsters.runningMonster: A small group of gargoyles of around 3-4 will provide a good threat against an average party. Gargoyles should start from a higher point, like at the top of a church or something to let them engage with Stone Form on their terms. Half Pierce attacks completely counter Stone Form, as they ignore the extra guard it gives and the gargoyle can’t react to the attacks at all while in it.
monsters.appearance: Gargoyles are medium sized creatures that at a first glance look like statues. Their skin is made of stone and they have a pair of small wings on their back.
monsters.habitat: Found in abandoned places made out of stone.
monsters.lore: Gargoyles are usually tied to an abandoned place made out of stone where they will lie dormant in their stone form until people approach. When living creatures get close enough, they will reveal themselves and attack them. The reason behind their hostility remains unclear, and most adventurers that don’t want to deal with them simply avoid their resting place.

monsters.name: Ghost
monsters.strategy:
The ghost will start by throwing objects at its enemies. Once it is engaged in combat, it will use Spectral Touch instead of heavy attacks when attacking an armored enemy.

Against a physical attack, it can always react for free thanks to its Incorporeal ability.
monsters.runningMonster: Ghost can be a pushover or almost impossible to fight depending on what the party has available. They are intended to operate in groups, but characters that rely purely on physical attacks will struggle to hit it, where as parties with casters or tools such as Sacrament will cut through the ghost without much issues.
monsters.appearance: The ghost's appearance mimics that of the person that died, except more transparent.
monsters.habitat: Can be found in any place where a person died.
monsters.lore: The ghost is an undead monster that spawned from a person that died while bearing a strong grudge. They are hostile to any living creature around them, mistaking them for the subject of their vengeance.

monsters.name: Ghoul
monsters.strategy:
If a ghoul can eat a corpse with Devour Corpse, it will always do so. It may even move to the corpse to do it if it can do so safely.

When in combat, it will use its Ghoul Bite if it can and it is missing HP. Otherwise, it will attack normally.
monsters.runningMonster: A large group of ghouls can make a good challenge for a group of adventurers. Ghouls become a lot more powerful if they fight in a room or place that has a lot of corpses ready to be devoured. Ghouls can also use Devour Corpse on the bodies of other ghouls.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature with grey skin, sharp teeth and red eyes.
monsters.habitat: Usually found in places with lots of dead bodies.
monsters.lore: Ghouls are undead that are perpetually hungry. They feed on the corpses of dead creatures, preferably humanoids.

monsters.name: Giant Astra Crab
monsters.strategy: It's very adaptive, e.g. it will try to counter its opponent's actions. However, it doesn't plan ahead, it simply reacts. It just wants food, and will try to escape death. Peaceful resolution may be possible with sufficiently large offerings?
monsters.runningMonster:
One giant crab is a good challenge for a group of 4 SC3000+ characters.

Gather Parts: DC25 to harvest a Perfect Shell.
monsters.appearance: A giant crab
monsters.habitat: Beaches in the astra line
monsters.lore:
The ultimate lifeform.

By Nya.

monsters.name: Giant Mantis
monsters.strategy:
At the start of the battle, it will leaping strike to the most vulnerable looking target it can safely reach. It will not provoke attacks of opportunity to do so.

Once it’s engaged in combat, it will keep attacking the most vulnerable looking target. It will use slice and dice whenever it can.
monsters.runningMonster:
The Giant Mantis can cut through unarmored targets extremely quickly if it gets a surprise round. If the party does not have high perception values, then it may be best to not run more than 2 at the same time. If running more than 2, it may be better to forego the stealth part.

Note that the Giant Mantis poses very little threat to an armored target, but it's danger level rises if the party has no armored people.
monsters.appearance: A giant mantis
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: A mantis the size of a regular person. Nobody knows how they grew so big.

monsters.name: Giant Prismatic Slime
monsters.strategy: If the slime is out of range to attack, it will use Bowling Roller. If it is in range to use Gluttony, it will do so. It will use Digestion when it can on the turn after it hits with Gluttony.
monsters.runningMonster: A solo monster against which regular attacks will do little. A group with heavy magic damage may be able to kill it normally, but dealing damage without landing a critical hit is nearly impossible. Make sure to give the players enough hints and guidance so that they can realize this.
monsters.appearance: A large slime in the colors of the rainbow.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere with astra influence.
monsters.lore: A fiend that appears like a giant slime. Seeks to devour the mana of other creatures.

monsters.name: Giant Spider
monsters.strategy: The Giant Spider will attempt to Web Spray the closest target if it is not in melee range. Afterwards, it will move up and attack using poison bite whenever it can.
monsters.runningMonster: A large group of giant spiders can provide a decent challenge to a group of adventurers. Should be combined with other grunt spiders to create a more varied encounter.
monsters.appearance: A large spider.
monsters.habitat: The giant spider is most commonly found underground or in caves where a broodmother has set up her lair.
monsters.lore: A large spider that preys on regular people.

monsters.name: Gravity Fiend
monsters.strategy:
The gravity fiend starts the combat by using Exousiai's Presence. On each of its turns it will use Weight of the World, followed by Gravity Crash if possible.

After that, it will use Gravity Pull to get enemies in range then use Crushing Presence if it can hit enough enemies.

It has high regeneration and is intelligent. If it is threatened, it can attempt to create distance to give it a turn to heal.
monsters.runningMonster:
The Gravity Fiend is not something you should use against a party and expect them to beat it without preparation. Against an unprepared party of people that are most likely running max burden, it can easily inflict heavy damage or kill people without much counterplay. Due to this, it is rated as danger level EX.

It functions as a solo monster against a whole party of 5 even when they do prepare. Against an average prepared party, this can be considered to be a D rated threat.
monsters.appearance: A floating ball of meat with 3 metal rings around it.
monsters.habitat: The corwood in the astra line
monsters.lore: An Exousiai with gravity powers.

monsters.name: Greater Astran Magpie
monsters.strategy: A greater astran magpie follows the targeting described in its Strike for the Shiny, smartly! ability. They use Swooping Strike II almost exclusively, unless they can attack without moving already.
monsters.runningMonster:
1 or 2 Greater Astran Magpie along with a large group of normal Astran Magpie's makes a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. While a greater astran magpie can be harder to hit than other enemies, keep in mind its damage out is comparatively lower than other heroic enemies.

Gather Parts: 250u of feathersteel from their talons, 250u of direhide from the pelt.
monsters.appearance: Two eyes on each side of its head (four total) otherwise looks like a larger magpie.
monsters.habitat: The astra line.
monsters.lore:
An astra corrupted magpie

By Mega Mike 70

monsters.name: Greater Manticore
monsters.strategy:
The greater manticore has 2 separate attack phases.

The first attack phase should be using the head to attack, starting with Lion's Roar and then attacking slowed targets to gain the bonuses from the crushing maw ability.

The second attack phase should use the tail, using Tail Spikes and then attacking targets that were hit by it if possible.
monsters.runningMonster:
The greater manticore is a solo monster that has a lot more AP than a normal creature would have thanks to its dual headed ability. You don't need to stick to the head and tail attack phases, but it will make it easier to run and for players to understand.

Gather Parts: 1000 units of primehide.
monsters.appearance: A large creature with the body of a lion, a scorpion like tail and a large pair of wings.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the wild or in a dungeon.
monsters.lore: The greater manticore is a monstrous combination of three different types of animal originally fused together through magic. They possess little intelligence and do little more than feast on anyone unfortunate enough to run into one. Their second head is a mutation caused by astra corruption that only makes it more vicious.

monsters.name: Gryphon
monsters.strategy:
The gryphon will stay in the sky and harrass with Wind Blast until its mana runs out. If it lands a hit and knocks a target prone, it will follow up with Dive Attack on the target.

If the enemy has a lot of ranged attackers or if they are too spread out for a Wind Blast, the gryphon might go in earlier with a Dive Attack and use regular attacks instead.
monsters.runningMonster:
A group of gryphons can challenge a group of seasoned adventurers.

Gather Parts: 500 units of Direhide.
monsters.appearance: The gryphon is a large creature has the body of a lion with the wings and head of an eagle.
monsters.habitat: Found in the mountains or other places with high elevation.
monsters.lore: The gryphon despite its appearance is an animal that naturally appears in the wild. They are territorial, but not hostile to people that stay far enough away from them.

monsters.name: Heliamphora
monsters.strategy:
The opening for a Heliamphora is to wait for a target to walk in range of its vines without noticing the plant. It may use Luring Pollen to do so.

After its surprise attack, it will try to put any grabbed creatures in its pitcher whenever possible. If any creatures are more than 10ft away from it, it will use its pollen to lure them closer. After that, it will try to grab as many creatures as possible using its basic attack and vine grab.
monsters.runningMonster:
Make sure the players are aware of the threat of the pitcher once a player has been grabbed by describing the creature as attempting to move the player to its pitcher. Being dropped in it takes a player out of the fight and may get them killed.

Some players may also need help in recognizing that they can destroy the vines. If you want to go easy on the players, you can delay the first drop in pot and drop hints that the vines can be targeted.
monsters.appearance: It appears like a giant pitcher plant.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere in a forest or similar area.
monsters.lore: The Heliamphora is a large pitcher plant, of which smaller versions are sometimes kept as house plants. It is effectively mindless, just luring in creatures with its pollen and attacking them to eat.

monsters.name: Hobgoblin Boar Rider
monsters.strategy: The boar rider will charge towards the enemy backline, aiming to trample as many enemies on the way there as possible.
monsters.runningMonster: A large group of boar riders will make a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. As they are a mounted enemy, boar riders excel in open fields and are worse indoors. They can also be combined with other Hobgoblin enemies for a more varied challenge.
monsters.appearance: A hobgoblin riding a boar
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Hobgoblins on a boar.

monsters.name: Hobgoblin Fighter
monsters.strategy:
A hobgoblin fighter hits the closest target it can reach. If there are multiple, it will hit the one with the least armor. If it cannot reach any target, it will throw a rock.

When a hobgoblin goes below half HP, it will use Gobbo Regeneration.
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of Hobgoblins enemies will provide a decent challenge to a group of adventurers starting out. 

It can only use its heal once due to the mana cost. You can also give some of them ranged weapons to create a more balanced enemy group.
monsters.appearance: A feral goblin.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Gobo

monsters.name: Hobgoblin Tactician
monsters.strategy:
The hobgoblin tactician uses its Stratagem: Lightning at the start of the encounter. When it loses more than 15 HP, it will use its Gobbo Regeneration.

The hobgoblin tactician is smarter than other hobgoblins and can move tactically to hit weaker enemies. It may also choose to take some damage early and save RP to be able to heal the damage up with its self healing.
monsters.runningMonster: The hobgoblin tactician is best matched with several hobgoblin fighters The tactician can speed up the fighters and get them in range. It uses a 2handed weapon for extra damage.
monsters.appearance: A feral goblin.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: A gobo tactician

monsters.name: Hydra
monsters.strategy: The hydra will open with their Hydra Breath attacks if the enemy isn’t in range, or if they can hit 3+ people with it. Otherwise, they will attempt a constrict into Three Headed Assault on a target when possible.
monsters.runningMonster:
The Hydra can serve as a solo monster for a party of 4. The regenerative nature of the heads can make it feel to the players that they are not making progress or doing the wrong thing, so make sure to emphasize that the hydra is being slowed and weakened when the heads grow.

The Hydra lacks a strong central body for the players to target, so you can just put 3-5 head tokens to represent the heads (it dies after getting 6+ heads). The heads shouldn’t move more than 5ft away from each other.

Gather Parts: 1000 units of Primehide
monsters.appearance: The hydra is a creature with three heads resting on a long neck attached to a rather small frame. It is usually found with its body below the water with only the three heads sticking out. The necks and heads are covered in colored scales with each of the heads having a different color that marks their element. The Earth one is green, the Frost one is white and the Lightning one is golden.
monsters.habitat: Almost always found near water. Due to the size of the hydra, usually a large river or lake.
monsters.lore: A weird animal that has three heads that each have their own thoughts. Each head itself is an intelligent creature (though they lack the ability to speak a common language), but the heads themselves are always in conflict. They struggle to make a decision on even the most basic things, sometimes resorting to infighting. Only when their existence is threatened by an outside source do the heads work together.

monsters.name: Ice Queen
monsters.strategy:
The ice queen will start by summoning a tower near her enemies with both her encounter start action and her normal ability, then immediately follow it up with Reverbant Frost.

She wants to keep away from melee enemies as much as possible. If she can escape them without provoking, she will do so. Future towers will be placed to either slow melee enemies on top of her, or in the biggest group of enemies. She will always follow up a tower placement with Reverbant Frost.

If she has the option to hit slowed enemies safely with Shards of Ice, she will do so. Otherwise she will attack with whatever weapon is most suitable for the situation. She can easily use a ranged weapon to safely attack more vulnerable opponents.
monsters.runningMonster:
The ice queen is a solo monster that is both intelligent and cunning. She may avoid direct fights if they don't appear to be in her favor or attempt to negotiate if things look dire.

Most of her threat comes from the towers. If players are dedicated to instantly destroying them, she may need reinforcements to keep up the threat.
monsters.appearance: A beautiful woman with pale or blue skin and white hair. Stands out from the average yuki-onna or frost maiden with her regal stature and the crown of ice she wears on her head.
monsters.habitat: Can be found in any place where it freezes for most of the year.
monsters.lore:
An ice elemental with high intelligence that commands other elementals and beasts in the area. She does this without directly communicating with them, merely her presence in the area is enough for ice creatures to submit.

She is domineering, but can be reasoned and negotiated with if shown the proper respect.

monsters.name: Inkblight
monsters.strategy:
The Inkblight moves forward hitting the target that looks the weakest. If targeted by an attack they can dodge, they will use their Inky Dodge to do so.

If they are in a position to use their Ink Attack, they will do so and use the strongest attack possible.
monsters.runningMonster:
A group of 16 inkblights are a suitable threat for an experienced group of 4 adventurers. Inkblights, like most fiends, are intelligent. They will target squishy looking targets and use their inky dodge to pressure ranged attackers with the teleport.

Recommended spirit core level: 2000-2500.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid shape of ink.
monsters.habitat: Storybooks.
monsters.lore: A fiend found in storybook dungeons.

monsters.name: Ixilune
monsters.lore:
Summoning Cost: 4 AP, 2 Mana

10x10ft size

monsters.name: Jack of Hearts
monsters.lore: 2 AP, 2 Mana to summon

monsters.name: Landshark
monsters.strategy:
Landsharks are extremely hard to hit while they are not attacking. They become vulnerable when they leap out to bite, allowing for readied attacks or other reaction attacks to hit them easily. 

Because ranged attackers cannot easily do this, they become the easiest target to focus on for Landsharks. If given the option, Landsharks should always aim to attack ranged attackers over melee ones. Landsharks do not provoke opportunity attacks, allowing them to swim past the melee line. Thus if they can reach a ranged attacker and attack them they should do so. Otherwise, they will attack the melee attacker closest to them if already in range and then swim away.
monsters.weakAgainst: Sure hit attacks, other Burrowed creatures
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of landsharks is a good challenge for a group of adventurers.

As a note, when a player makes a readied action against the Landshark to hit it when it comes up, the readied attack will go off first.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hides
monsters.appearance: A small creature with a large fin.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the wild. Most common in open fields.
monsters.lore: The landshark is a small beast that travels below the ground and attacks travelers.

monsters.name: Mage
monsters.strategy:
Mages prefer to stay in the back, using either Glittershards to block off enemy ranged attackers or using Arcane Net to entrap enemy melee attackers. Possibly both. Afterwards, they will use Missile Barrage to soften up all enemies. Depending on their allies and the battle situation, mages may want to retain some mana to recast the net or glittershards. 

If they are under threat, they will want to reserve 1 mana to make Block a valid option. A mage engaged in melee combat can’t do much, they will have to disengage and move away.
monsters.runningMonster:
Mages are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being both a ranged controller and AoE striker. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Apprentice’ generic enemy.

Mages can function with Grunt level allies, though they will need to be set up in situations where their control abilities can shine. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Mages generally use a channeling weapon and wear no armor.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Mages are spellcasters without a specialization. They are the most common type of mage, though most will soon specialize in an element or magic type. They exist in every race, though human mages are the rarest ones.

monsters.name: Mana Slime
monsters.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Arcanium flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Arcane Herb.
monsters.appearance: A small cute slime.
monsters.lore:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

monsters.name: Manticore
monsters.strategy: The manticore will open with Lion's roar. If it managed to slow any targets, it will focus on that target with its crushing maw. If no enemies were affected by the roar or if there's no enemies in range to attack, it will use tail spikes. Afterwards, it wil attack with the tail.
monsters.runningMonster:
The manticore can be run together with 3 other heroic creatures to make a good challenge.

Gather Parts: 500 units of direhide.
monsters.appearance: A large creature with the body of a lion, a scorpion like tail and a large pair of wings.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the wild or in a dungeon.
monsters.lore: The manticore is a monstrous combination of three different types of animal originally fused together through magic. They possess little intelligence and do little more than feast on anyone unfortunate enough to run into one.

monsters.name: Minotaur
monsters.strategy: The minotaur will use all their AP on Goring Charge if not in range of an enemy. Once in range, they will attack normally and use Headbutt when they can.
monsters.runningMonster: A group of minotaurs provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Its stats are fairly high, but its abilities are unimpressive and it mostly just basic attacks.
monsters.appearance: A creature with the body of a man and the head of a bull.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere in the world.
monsters.lore: A creature often confused with the chimera of Northi. Despite a similar appearance, the original minotaur is a cursed creature once locked away in a labyrinth. Its offspring now roam the world, causing destruction wherever they go.

monsters.name: Ogre
monsters.strategy: The ogre will use Smash you and Smash you more whenever it can, attacking the nearest enemy.
monsters.runningMonster: A group of ogres provides a good challenge for a group of adventurers.
monsters.appearance: A huge humanoid with a rugged look. An ogre can easily be 10 foot tall.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: A huge humanoid monster that possess some form of intelligence similar to that of a human child. They are often easily tricked by skilled manipulators who use them for their own goals.

monsters.name: Pipoltr
monsters.lore:
Summon cost: 4 AP, 4 Mana

10x10ft size

monsters.name: Priest
monsters.strategy:
A priest will want to play close to the frontlines to be in range for Angel’s Embrace. Once the melee’s of each side have engaged on combat, the priest can drop a hallowed ground in such a way that it affects all of their melee allies. Afterwards, they will focus on attacking and will use their remaining mana to cast Cure Touch once an ally (heroic allies only if there is any left) becomes low on HP.

Angel’s Embrace can be used to absorb big hits on allies, though the priest should stop using it unless to prevent a killing blow once their own RP becomes too low.
monsters.runningMonster:
Priests are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being both a support and healer. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Acolyte’ generic enemy.

Priests can function with Grunt level allies, though their support will not be nearly as effective as when supporting heroic allies. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Priests can use either a channeling weapon or a light melee weapon + shield. Priests can wear anything from no armor, light armor to medium armor. In the stat block above, a light melee weapon + shield and light armor is assumed.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Priests are spellcasters that draw their power from the gods. Due to the popularity and strength of Kari, the human goddess, the vast majority of priests in the world are human. However, priests of other races do still exist. Some may follow Kari, while others may follow their own god or goddess.

monsters.name: Raiju
monsters.strategy:
The Raiju's strategy is the same regardless of whether its storming or not. It will start by using Static Field at encounter start.

On its turn, it will use Static Charge to pass through as many enemies as it can, without having to move before using Lightning Charge. The remaining AP will be used on attacking.
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of Raiju will provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. During a storm, you'll want to lower the amount if you want to keep the difficulty similar as the same group of Raiju can quickly murder a group of low level adventurers.

If it is hunting one of the party members, you can have the Raiju focus on that party member even at risk to themselves.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hide.
monsters.appearance: A white wolf like creature around which electricity constantly crackles.
monsters.habitat: Rarely found anywhere in the wild. Only seen by those it is hunting.
monsters.lore:
The raiju is often confused for an animal due to its appearance. In reality, its an elemental that serves as the hunting dog for a more powerful elemental creature. It will track and hound an enemy from afar, then move in for the kill once the weather changes.

Storms have an unnaturally high chance of appearing when this creature is around.

monsters.name: Rhinoceros Beetle
monsters.lore: Summon cost: 3 AP, 2 Mana.

monsters.name: Rime Vermin
monsters.strategy: The Rime Vermin uses Self Icicle Nail to get in range if it can. When in range to attack, it will use Heavy attacks if it can and otherwise will just use Light attacks.
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of around 16 rime vermin makes a challenging fight for a group of 4. You can replace 4 of these to replace them with a heroic unit that might benefit from the ice the rime vermin create. 

Gather Parts: Using gather parts nets a Rime Vermin Ball, which functions like an Elemental Mixture Flask (Frost) and is worth 200 Clim.
monsters.appearance: A small creature made out of ice.
monsters.habitat: Found in area's with lots of snow and ice.
monsters.lore: An artificially made elemental creature that was created by a powerful Yuki Onna. Often is disguised as regular ice, but too slow to take advantage of any surprises.

monsters.name: Rogue
monsters.strategy: Rogues aim for the backline, targeting enemy mages or archers. They can slip past the frontlines using Feint and can avoid enemy attacks by using their 0 RP evasive maneuver. If an enemy is at 0 RP, they can move to that enemy and use their Devastating Strike on them.
monsters.runningMonster:
Rogue are intended to be generic grunt enemies that focus on skirmishing. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the grunt version of the ‘Assassin’ generic enemy.

Rogues can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

Rogues prefer light or no armor along with a pair of light weapons, usually daggers.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Rogues are shifty individuals that use trickery and dirty tactics to win battles. They exist in every race and society.

monsters.name: Skeletal Champion
monsters.appearance: An armored skeleton wielding a greatsword.
monsters.lore: A skeleton warrior summoned by necromancers.

monsters.name: Skeletal Monstrosity
monsters.strategy:
The Skeletal Monstrosity’s battle strategy is simple. It will attack a random target (or the target that did the most damage to it the previous round) and use Skeletal Armblade Barrage. Afterwards, it will use the sweep against the largest group of targets. After those two attacks, it will keep making light and heavy attacks as appropriate.

If there are no enemies in his attack range, which is 10ft, it will use Bone Spike Shot until an enemy is pulled within its range, then continue with the above mentioned strategy.
monsters.runningMonster:
The Skeletal Monstrosity is a good enemy to face by itself. Against stronger parties, you can add a few normal skeletons to the mix or give the creature additional arms to further boost its action economy.

Token wise, you want to have a bigger token for the main body (10x10ft token) and then 4 5x5ft tokens for each of the arms. The arms should be adjacent to the main body in some way.
monsters.appearance: A large skeletal creature that has 2 pairs of extra arms. It sits low to the floor and uses one of the pairs of arms to support its weight. Despite this, it still towers above the average person. Their frontal arms are sharpened into blades instead of having hands.
monsters.habitat: Usually found in places a necromancer has been.
monsters.lore: These creatures are created by skilled necromancers and due to their regenerative abilities will often out live their masters. Though they are mindless, their former instructions still linger and they are likely to attack any creatures that approach it.

monsters.name: Skeleton
monsters.strategy: The skeletons attacks the nearest target.
monsters.runningMonster: The skeleton is a very weak monster, especially against groups that possess bludgeoning attacks. A large group of skeletons is needed to provide a good challenge for a group of adventurers.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid skeleton.
monsters.habitat: Usually found in places a necromancer has been.
monsters.lore: Skeletons are the bones of people long dead that have been reanimated, usually through necromancy but rarely through astra corruption. They are mindless undead, swinging a weapon - often times a bone of themselves - at the closest living creature they see.

monsters.name: Slime
monsters.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Alchemy units.
monsters.appearance: A small cute slime.
monsters.lore:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

monsters.name: Sniper
monsters.strategy:
The sniper’s strategy in combat is to sit still as far away as possible and do damage to the most vulnerable target. What the most vulnerable target is may change during the course of the battle and a sniper can easily adapt to the situation.

They can use Homing Shot when dealing with high dodge characters. If they are engaged in melee combat, they will use Disengaging Shot if they have mana for it. If they don’t, the common strategy is to switch to a melee weapon.
monsters.runningMonster:
Snipers are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on ranged combat. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Archer’ generic enemy.

Snipers can be run together with several grunt level enemies or in a group together with around 3 similar heroic enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Snipers can use any type of ranged weapon, though pistols, shotguns and sniper rifles are rarely seen. Snipers often wear no or light armor. Most will also carry a melee weapon as a backup weapon.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Sniper is a title given to all users of ranged weaponry that display some level of skill. They exist in every race and can use a wide variety of ranged weapons.

monsters.name: Tactician
monsters.notableSkills: Knowledge History+11, Perception+10, Negotiation+11, Intimidation+11, Deception+10
monsters.strategy: The tactician relies mostly on their troops to do the damage. Their job is to apply Focus Fire to the target most vulnerable or which is reachable by the most of their troops. They can use reposition to cut off escapes or make their allies easily reach the backline. They will always use Stratagem: Lightning at the start of the encounter.
monsters.runningMonster:
Tacticians are intended to be generic heroic enemies that focus on tactics and leadership. They can easily be used for any race or situation that requires it.

A tactician is worthless without a good number of grunt level allies. They can pair well with both melee attackers with Stratagem: Lightning and Reposition, but also ranged attackers due to easier Focus Fire usage.

With Battle Tactics, you are free to play the enemies as smartly as you can, roleplaying it as the tactician giving precise orders. Tacticians can use a wide variety of weapons and armor depending on the race or society they are from. Ranged weapons are generally preferable, as a tactician going down may lead to an instant loss.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Tacticians are found in virtually every society and can be of any race. Oftentimes, but not always, they are leaders such as a captain, general or something simpler like a bandit chief. They lead their troops to victory not always through charisma, but through tactics.

monsters.name: Tank
monsters.strategy: The tank’s strategy is to move up to take space, then provoke the closest melee enemy he can.
monsters.runningMonster:
Tanks are intended to be generic grunt enemies that focus on being a tanky frontline. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Defender’ generic enemy.

Tank can function with around 10 other Grunt level allies and 1 heroic ally to pose a light threat to a party. Can be combined with other generic enemies to create a balanced composition.

The above stat block assumes they are using Medium Armor and a Shield. Any melee weapon can work for a tank
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Tanks are front liners who go in first and absorb the hits for their allies. Existing in every culture and of any race, they are usually heavily armored with shields.

monsters.name: Troll
monsters.strategy: The troll simply attacks the nearest target. It should only react to Heavy attacks.
monsters.runningMonster: A group of trolls provide a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Its stats are fairly high, but its abilities are unimpressive and it mostly just basic attacks.
monsters.appearance: A large ugly humanoid.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore:
Trolls descend from what were once regular humans that mutated into these hideous creatures. 

In a way, they are similar to what hobgoblins are to normal goblins. Perhaps because of this, they are often found in the company of them.

monsters.name: Unstable Efreet
monsters.strategy: Unstable Efreet’s strategy is very simple. They will run towards the nearest enemy and attack them until they die and explode.
monsters.runningMonster: For the most effective use, Unstable Efreets should not start too far away from the players, otherwise they might cause a chain reaction of explosions before they get in range. Be careful when putting these against a Pyromancer. Pyromancers can trivialize this encounter by tagging them with fire spells, but if they do it while the Unstable Efreets are too close, then they could cause a chain reaction that leads to a constant barrage of explosions on the players.
monsters.appearance: A creature of pure fire and flame that appears roughly in a humanoid shape.
monsters.habitat: Found near Efreets.
monsters.lore: Unstable Efreets are split off parts of a normal Efreet. Their very existence is a fleeting thing with them being able to exist for little more than day before their flames going out and them vanishing into nothingness.

monsters.name: Warrior
monsters.strategy: Warriors use Charge to engage the frontline in combat and hit the most vulnerable target there. If engaged with two or more enemies, they will use Cleaving Strike. Else, they will use Skullsplitter if the target is wearing at least medium armor.
monsters.runningMonster:
Warriors are intended to be a base for generic heroic enemies that focus on being a hardhitting melee. They can be used for any race or situation and can easily be added to fit what you need. They are the heroic version of the ‘Brute’ generic enemy.

Warriors can function with Grunt level allies, but they will want some tank type allies to not get focused down as hard. They can function in a group with around 3 generic heroic level enemies like the Defender, Assassin etc.

Warriors generally use heavy melee weapons. They can use no armor, light armor or medium armor depending on the race. The stat block above assumes light armor and a heavy melee weapon. Some might carry a ranged weapon as backup.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature.
monsters.habitat: Can be found anywhere.
monsters.lore: Warriors are combatants that specialize in melee combat. They exist in every race and civilization and can use a wide variety of weapons and armor.

monsters.name: Water Slime
monsters.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Vivinthal flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Water Herb.
monsters.appearance: A small cute slime.
monsters.lore:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

monsters.name: Westrian Heavy Paladin
monsters.strategy: Westrian Heavy Paladins aim to charge towards the enemy backline with mounted charge, aiming to move through as many enemies as possible to get there. Once they are in melee range, they will use Divine Smite on each of their turns while their mana lasts. As Divine Shield is free, they will use it at the start of each turn.
monsters.runningMonster:
A small group of around 4 heavy paladins would make a challenging encounter for a group of players. As they are mounted enemies, they benefit from an open fighting field and are unsuitable for indoor fights.

Heavy Paladins are intelligent creatures and veteran fighters. Don't be afraid to play them intelligently. If a paladin can hit a demon in their divine release state with their divine smite, they should always do so unless it would cause them to provoke too many attacks.
monsters.appearance: A heavily armored man or woman riding an armored mount.
monsters.habitat: Westria
monsters.lore: To do.

monsters.name: Wight
monsters.strategy: The wight will attacks the closest target. It can choose between Spectral Touch or Draining Touch + a light attack, both are valid options.
monsters.runningMonster:
Wights are very strong against physical attackers. Even a small group of wights can be annoying to fight when you don't have any non-physical damage. Consider the party's abilities very carefully when choosing how many wights to put in.

You can choose to have Wights use their RP immediately, which opens them up for physical attackers, or have them save their RP so they can always react to the physical attackers. The first option will make the fight more manageable for the party members who don't have magical damage options.
monsters.appearance: A translucent white creature with a vaguely humanoid shape.
monsters.habitat: Appears around places where a Wraith is.
monsters.lore: When a creature is slain by a Wraith, there's a high chance a Wight will be born from its corpse. Wights are automatically subservient to the Wraith that killed them and must stay within a mile radius of it or disappear entirely.

monsters.name: Wind Slime
monsters.runningMonster:
About 4 slimes per player would make an adequate challenge for parties. Parties with only physical damage will struggle against slimes.

Gather Parts: 250u of Sylphsteel flamellons. With a check of at least 20 may also choose to gather the core, which functions as a Rare Wind Herb.
monsters.appearance: A small cute slime.
monsters.lore:
Just a slime.

By Nya.

monsters.name: Wolf
monsters.strategy: The wolves will try to swarm a target, though they won't take attacks of opportunity to do so. They will keep using topple prey until the target is prone, then the other wolves will use go for the throat.
monsters.runningMonster:
A large group of wolves will make a good challenge for a group of adventurers, ideally led by an Alpha Wolf. All wolves move at the same time to let them gain a huge bonus to their hit rolls before attacking.

Gather Parts: 250 units of animal hide.
monsters.appearance: A normal wolf
monsters.habitat: Usually found in a forest.
monsters.lore: A normal wolf. Occasionally kept as pet.

monsters.name: Wraith
monsters.strategy:
The Wraith will avoid bright light the best it can, only going in if it has no other choice. It may use Darkness in this case to negate the effects of it if possible.

If it doesn't need to avoid bright light, it will use Darkness after spending 3 AP, then immediately follow up with Darkness Shade to hide.

For attacks, it will use the Spectral Touch and Draining Touch. Like other incorporeal enemies, it can freely react to any physical attacks without burning RP.
monsters.runningMonster:
A group of wraith's can provide a good challenge to a high spirit core party. At this point, most people should have a way of dealing non-physical weapon. The wraith's stats are a bit higher than the other incorporeal enemies, so be careful because some members of the party may have 0 chance of hitting it even with that.

Having a source of bright light also helps the players. A torch alone wouldn't qualify, but a northi lantern or a paladin's holy weapon might.
monsters.appearance: A translucent dark creature with a vaguely humanoid shape.
monsters.habitat: Found only in permanently dark places.
monsters.lore: A vengeful spirit that died in the darkness while it was still alive. Brought back to life through a necromancer or through astra corruption, they attack any living creature that they can see. They are weak to bright lights and will never willingly go into the sunlight.

monsters.name: Wyrm (Fire)
monsters.strategy:
The firewyrm will rain fire from the sky until it is forced down to the ground or it runs out of mana. Even when out of mana, it may still choose to do fly-by attacks instead of staying on the ground.

While in the sky, it can use both Fireball and Flame Breath at the largest group of enemies. On the ground, it will use tail swipe as the final action of each round and may still use flame breath if it has mana left.

At the encounter start, it will always use Terrifying Roar.
monsters.runningMonster:
The firewyrm is a solo monster that is a serious threat to any party without aeromancers. In a space where their flight is limited, they can be less threatening. As they are intelligent creatures, a firewyrm may retreat if the battle starts going badly for it.

The firewyrm is bigger than a drake, but the token size is still the same.

Gather Parts: 1000 units of dragonscale.
monsters.appearance: A large scaled lizard with a pair of wings on its back.
monsters.habitat: Most commonly found high in the mountain in places with a warm temperature.
monsters.lore: A distant relative of the dragons that have vanished. Though they spent most of their time sleeping in their caves, they are hostile to all living creatures and view them are little more than prey. Wyrms are older, more intelligent and more dangerous than their Drake and Wyrmling counterparts.

monsters.name: Zombies
monsters.strategy: Zombies move towards the near enemy. If the target is not already grabbed (by any zombie) and they can make a Heavy attack, they make a Heavy attack. Otherwise if they are not already grabbing an enemy, they will do so.
monsters.runningMonster: A large group of zombies is a decent challenge for a group of adventurers. Zombies are weak to holy damage, so you will want to add more of them to keep the challenge the same when the players have classes like a paladin or priest with them. Zombies are slow, but relatively tanky for a grunt enemy. Against parties that are less likely to exploit this weakness or if fighting in a place where its impossible to do, you may want to use slightly less zombies.
monsters.appearance: A humanoid creature with decaying skin.
monsters.habitat: Found in places with corpses or near necromancers.
monsters.lore: Mindless corpses resurrected through necromancy or astra corruption.

monsterAbilities.name: Absorb Magic
monsterAbilities.description: When you take Arcane, Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Holy or Dark damage or any of its subtypes, you charge your crystals. Your next Crystal Stomp does additional damage equal to the Power of the attacker and the damage type of it changes to the type you took. Does not stack.

monsterAbilities.name: Alchemic Engine Overdrive
monsterAbilities.description: This creature gaines +2 extra AP at the start of every turn after its been reduced to less than 50% HP.

monsterAbilities.name: Animal Shield
monsterAbilities.description: When a creature you summoned is within 5ft of you, you may change the target of any attack targeting you to that creature instead. Only works if the creature isn’t already targeted as part of the attack.

monsterAbilities.name: Arcane Barrier
monsterAbilities.description: When taking the Block action while you have at least 1 mana, your Guard is increased by an additional 8.

monsterAbilities.name: Arcane Body
monsterAbilities.description: Your attacks may deal Physical or Arcane damage. When you deal Arcane damage, the target loses 1 MP though they get to make a Save if this was a light attack. Furthermore, any target ending its turn while rooted by your Consume loses 1 MP.

monsterAbilities.name: Arcane Type II
monsterAbilities.description: You take half damage from Arcane attacks or damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Armored Chitin
monsterAbilities.description: When using the Block reaction, gain +5 guard (Added into the stats already).

monsterAbilities.name: Aurasense
monsterAbilities.description: You can perfectly detect any creature within 120ft with a spirit core higher than 100.

monsterAbilities.name: Battle Tactics
monsterAbilities.description: All Grunt level allies under your command  will fight more intelligently, being more likely to target enemies that are weak or out of position

monsterAbilities.name: Berserker
monsterAbilities.description: Upon being reduced to half HP, you go into a tantrum like rage. While in this state, increase your Power by 2. If you are Stunned or Weakened this state will end for the rest of combat.

monsterAbilities.name: Black Mount
monsterAbilities.description: You are riding on a mount. The mount has a separate 75 HP, uses your defensive stats and follows normal horse mount rules. While mounted, you can only move in a straight line while taking a movement action. After losing your mount, your movement speed is reduced to 20ft. While above 0 HP, your mount heals for your Toughness HP at the start of your turn.

monsterAbilities.name: Bludgeoning Weakness
monsterAbilities.description: You take double damage from Bludgeoning weapons.

monsterAbilities.name: Boar Charger
monsterAbilities.description: When under the Trample effect, you can trample enemies the same size as you (Medium). You also deal an additional Power damage with the attack.

monsterAbilities.name: Boar Hide
monsterAbilities.description: You gain a +1 bonus to your guard and +2 bonus to Block (already added to stats).

monsterAbilities.name: Boar Mount
monsterAbilities.description: You are riding on a boar mount. The boar mount has a separate 10 HP and follows normal boar mount rules. While mounted, you can only move in a straight line while taking a movement action. After losing your mount, your movement speed is reduced to 20ft.

monsterAbilities.name: Burrow
monsterAbilities.description: You move underground at your normal speed. You do not provoke attacks of opportunities except from other burrowed creatures.

monsterAbilities.name: Calm Aim
monsterAbilities.description: If you didn’t move since the start of your last turn, you gain a +1d4 bonus to all accuracy checks.

monsterAbilities.name: Camouflage
monsterAbilities.description: You are hidden with a Stealth of 30 while pretending to be an ordinary plant until you attack. Luring Pollen does not break camouflage and will not trigger combat when used while creatures are unaware of you.

monsterAbilities.name: Combat Healer
monsterAbilities.description: Your Healing spells do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

monsterAbilities.name: Controlled Space
monsterAbilities.description: If you make an attack of opportunity, you can make a Heavy attack for 0 RP instead of 1. You gain a +2 bonus to accuracy checks when making attacks of opportunity.

monsterAbilities.name: Core Brain
monsterAbilities.description: Critical attacks deal 125 bonus true damage to you.

monsterAbilities.name: Creature of Fire
monsterAbilities.description: You take half damage from all fire damage and your attacks deal fire damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Crushing Maw
monsterAbilities.description: When making a basic Light or Heavy attack with your maw, you become enhanced against Slowed targets. If it’s a Light attack, you gain Sure Hit. If it’s a Heavy attack, you gain Full Pierce.

monsterAbilities.name: Deathtouch
monsterAbilities.description: A non-heroic creature reduced to 0 HP by you immediately rises as a Wight after 24 hours have passed.

monsterAbilities.name: Double Headed
monsterAbilities.description: You take two turns. Regardless of initiative, your first turn always comes first in a round. Your second turn comes after half of your enemies have taken their turn.

monsterAbilities.name: Dragon Fire
monsterAbilities.description: When you inflict Burning on a target that is already suffering from Burning, they immediately take Fire damage equal to the existing Burning value.

monsterAbilities.name: Earth Body
monsterAbilities.description: Your attacks may deal Earth or Physical damage. When you deal Earth damage, the target must make a Save or becomes Slowed until the end of their next turn.

monsterAbilities.name: Earth Immunity
monsterAbilities.description: You take no damage from Earth damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Earth Type II
monsterAbilities.description: You take half damage from Earth and Lightning attacks or damage, but you take 50% more from Wind type attacks and damage. You also take half damage from physical attacks, but your movement speed is halved.

monsterAbilities.name: Elite Solo Aura
monsterAbilities.description: You gain a +1 bonus to saves.

monsterAbilities.name: Evasive Rogue
monsterAbilities.description: You may use Evasive Maneuver for 0 RP instead of its normal cost.

monsterAbilities.name: Faewolf Shimmer
monsterAbilities.description: Your form appears half-real in dim or moonlit settings. You begin an encounter hidden unless spotted with a Perception check (e.g., DC 23). If forced into bright light, or if you makes noise (like a howl), the GM can allow another Perception roll to detect it.

monsterAbilities.name: Feeding Time
monsterAbilities.description: At the end of your turn, you deal a base 1 true damage + 1 true damage to all enemies for each part of your token that is touching the target.

monsterAbilities.name: Fire Body
monsterAbilities.description: Your attacks may deal Fire or Physical damage. When you deal Fire damage, you also inflict Burning 2*X where X is your Power. Furthermore, any target ending its turn while rooted by your Consume takes light Fire damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Fire Immunity
monsterAbilities.description: You take no damage from Fire damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Fire Resistance
monsterAbilities.description: You take only half damage from all fire damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Fire Type II
monsterAbilities.description: You take half damage from Fire and Frost attacks or damage, but you take 50% more from Water type attacks and damage. You are immune to Burning.

monsterAbilities.name: Fire Vulnerability
monsterAbilities.description: Fire damage dealt to you is treated as Full Pierce damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Fire Weakness
monsterAbilities.description: You take double damage from Fire damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Flight
monsterAbilities.description:
You can Fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so.

If you take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, your altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce your altitude to the point where you touch the ground, you become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from an flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.

monsterAbilities.name: Fly-by
monsterAbilities.description: You can fly through the air as if you were moving on land and your movement speed is doubled while doing so. While flying, you may make any of your attacks (spending AP as normal) during your movement and continue to move afterwards.

monsterAbilities.name: Frost Creation: Weapons
monsterAbilities.description: You may create any weapon and use it immediately. You are considered proficient in any weapon created through this ability. These weapons may deal Frost damage instead of their normal damage. You may also create two weapons at the same time, but they must be two Light weapons of the same type. You may dismiss these weapons at any time for no cost.

monsterAbilities.name: Gel Body
monsterAbilities.description: You cannot use basic defensive actions: Block or Dodge, but you have 100 Damage Reduction to all non-magical attacks.

monsterAbilities.name: Gravity Well
monsterAbilities.description: All enemies within 40ft of you are slowed. This applies immediately when they enter this range and lasts for the entire movement of leaving this range.

monsterAbilities.name: Growing Sludge
monsterAbilities.description: If you did not move in your last turn, your AP recovery and maximum AP increase by 1 (up to a maximum of 1).

monsterAbilities.name: Halberd
monsterAbilities.description: You have 10ft reach, but your weapon is otherwise treated as a Light axe.

monsterAbilities.name: Hard Shell
monsterAbilities.description: You have +1 guard and +4 Block, but -2 Evasion (already added to stats). You also have 5 DR against slashing attacks.

monsterAbilities.name: Hardened Scales
monsterAbilities.description: You gain +1 Guard, and a further +2 Guard when taking the Block action (Already added to stats).

monsterAbilities.name: Hardened Skin Mutation
monsterAbilities.description: Your guard is increased by 2.

monsterAbilities.name: Head Limit
monsterAbilities.description: Each head that grows extra past the original 3 lowers your agility by 1 and movement speed by 5ft. When your agility reaches 0 because of this, you die.

monsterAbilities.name: Head or Tails
monsterAbilities.description: When making a basic Light or Heavy Attack, you may attack with either your head or tail. You gain a benefit based on the body part chosen.

monsterAbilities.name: Head Regrowth
monsterAbilities.description: When a head is killed, two new heads immediately sprout from the defeated heads. These new heads share the element of the original defeated heads and function as two fresh heads as described in the multi-headed ability.

monsterAbilities.name: Heavy Cavalry
monsterAbilities.description: You have a mount that has 25 HP and uses your defensive stats in combat. It follows the normal horse mount rules. While mounted, you can only move in a straight line while taking a movement action. After losing your mount, your movement speed is reduced to 20ft.

monsterAbilities.name: Heavy Paws
monsterAbilities.description: When you deal damage to a target, they become Unbalanced. If they are already Unbalanced, they become Dazed.

monsterAbilities.name: High Flock Tactics
monsterAbilities.description: You gain a +1 bonus to your accuracy rolls (max +6) for each other Astran Magpie attacking the same target this round.

monsterAbilities.name: Holy Vulnerability
monsterAbilities.description: Holy damage dealt to you is treated as Full Pierce damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Holy Weakness
monsterAbilities.description: You take double damage from Holy damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Host Defense
monsterAbilities.description: When you become the target of an attack, the creature you are burrowed in takes the damage as well, even if you dodge the attack. Any damage you take is reduced by your host’s Guard against the attack. If the host takes damage from an area attack, you are also automatically hit.

monsterAbilities.name: Hover
monsterAbilities.description: You can passively hover up to 5ft above the ground. While hovering, you are not an eligible target for abilities that require a target to be flying or airborne unless you'd meet those conditions normally.

monsterAbilities.name: Hydra Elements
monsterAbilities.description: Each head has an element. There is an Earth, a Frost, and a Lightning element head. Each head takes half damage from attacks dealing the same type of damage as their element. Their element also influences their Hydra Breath attack.

monsterAbilities.name: Ice Defense
monsterAbilities.description: You provoke no attacks of opportunity from Slowed enemies. You gain a +4 bonus to Guard when taking the Block reaction. (Already added to stats)

monsterAbilities.name: Ice Immunity
monsterAbilities.description: You take no damage from Frost damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Ice Resistance
monsterAbilities.description: You take half damage from Frost damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Icy Puddle
monsterAbilities.description: When killed, the spot you were killed on turns into ice and becomes difficult terrain for other creatures.

monsterAbilities.name: Incorporeal
monsterAbilities.description: You do not spend your RP when reacting against a physical attack made with a non-magical weapon. A weapon that is enchanted counts as magical.

monsterAbilities.name: Ink Explosion
monsterAbilities.description: When you die, you explode in a blob of ink. You Blind all enemies and create difficult terrain in a 5ft radius around you.

monsterAbilities.name: Insatiable Hunger
monsterAbilities.description: You can use Gluttony as an attack of opportunity for 1 RP.

monsterAbilities.name: Ixilune's Chitin
monsterAbilities.description: You have +2 guard and +6 Block (already added to stats).

monsterAbilities.name: Just a nightmare
monsterAbilities.description: The dreameater only attacks sleeping targets and a battle against the dream eater does not take place in the physical world, but in a dreamscape created by it. A creature that is ‘killed’ by the dreameater does not die. Instead, they do not gain the normal benefits of resting and their mana is reduced by 2. If their mana would go below 0 because of this, they instead lose 5 Max HP per mana that could not be reduced. This effect lasts until the creature completes a rest undisturbed by the dreameater or until the dreameater dies.

monsterAbilities.name: Keen II
monsterAbilities.description: You land a critical hit when you roll 18 or higher.

monsterAbilities.name: Large Nimble Flier
monsterAbilities.description: You do not lose altitude for being hit while flying. However, you count as mounted for anti-mount abilities such as Brace.

monsterAbilities.name: Last Resort
monsterAbilities.description: When your HP is lowered to 0, you will immediately use Explode Self as a reaction. After that, you immediately die.

monsterAbilities.name: Lead the pack
monsterAbilities.description: You always act right before other wolves do. Their initiative is placed as 0.1 higher than that of normal wolves. When you are alive at the encounter start phase, wolves act first in the case of a tied initiative.

monsterAbilities.name: Leadership
monsterAbilities.description: All Grunt level allies under your command gain a +1 bonus to their Focus and Agility.

monsterAbilities.name: Lesser Fiend Regeneration
monsterAbilities.description: You heal for Toughness HP at the start of your turn.

monsterAbilities.name: Light Array Barrier
monsterAbilities.description: This creature has 40 block, but cannot dodge.

monsterAbilities.name: Light Vulnerability
monsterAbilities.description: If you are in an area with a bright light, become Weakened.

monsterAbilities.name: Lightning Immunity
monsterAbilities.description: You take no damage from Lightning damage.

monsterAbilities.name: Limited Dreaming
monsterAbilities.description: While in a dreamspace created by a dreameater, all abilities that have restrictions such as “Can only be used once per X.” or “You regain the use of this ability after a rest.” cannot be used. The exception to this is abilities that say “Can only be used once per encounter.” or “You regain the use of this ability at the Encounter Conclusion Phase”.

monsterAbilities.name: Limited Flight
monsterAbilities.description: You may fly during your movement at your normal speed, but if you are still airborne at the end of your turn, you fall to the ground taking fall damage as normal.

monsterAbilities.name: Low Flock Tactics
monsterAbilities.description: You gain a +1 bonus to your accuracy rolls (max +3) for each other Astran Magpie attacking the same target this round. All Astran Magpie's take their turn at the same time.

monsterAbilities.name: Luck Aura
monsterAbilities.description: When an ally within 60ft rolls a 1, they may automatically reroll that roll and accept the new result.

monsterAbilities.name: Medium Fiend Regeneration
monsterAbilities.description: You heal for Toughness x 3 HP at the start of your turn.

monsterAbilities.name: Mindless
monsterAbilities.description: You are immune to all mind-affecting effects.

monsterAbilities.name: Minor Hardened Skin Mutation
monsterAbilities.description: You gain +1 Guard.

monsterAbilities.name: Morale Failure
monsterAbilities.description: When your HP reaches 0 or lower, all Grunt level allies under your command experience Morale Failure. Unless there is another Heroic level ally on the battlefield, all Grunt level allies will attempt to flee the battlefield, potentially instantly ending the encounter.

monsterAbilities.name: Multi-headed
monsterAbilities.description: You have 3 heads, each with their own HP and element. Each head has 2 AP, 3 RP and they all use the same stats as listed in the stats block. Roll separate initiative for each head. An AoE attack only does damage to one of the heads, chosen by the attacker.

monsterAbilities.name: No Escape
monsterAbilities.description: You may use Burrow as an opportunity attack for 0 RP.

monsterAbilities.name: Overheat
monsterAbilities.description: When you take fire damage, you will start to explode. At the end of your next turn, your HP will be set to 0 and you will use Explode Self.

monsterAbilities.name: Pack Tactics
monsterAbilities.description: For each other Wolf adjacent to the target, a Wolf gets a +2 bonus to accuracy rolls on attacks against that target.

monsterAbilities.name: Petrifying Gaze
